articles.title: Unbeaten Utah Hosts BYU In A Holy War That Could Shape The Big 12 Title Race
articles.summary: The final month of the college football season in the Big 12 will shake loose a tight race and determine the teams that will play in the championship game.
articles.body: A Holy War starting in the breakfast hour is going to set the stage for a furious finish in the Big 12. No. 3 Utah hosts No. 7 BYU in what should go a long way toward determining a spot in the Dec. 4 conference championship game in Arlington, Texas. The tight league race will come down to whether the Utes (8-0, 5-0 Big 12) can hold onto their first-place perch with second-place BYU and No. 13 Texas Tech lurking. The Cougars and Red Raiders both are 7-1 and 4-1 in the conference, and another loss could jeopardize their chances of playing for a title and making the 12-team College Football Playoff. Texas Tech does not play BYU or Utah during the regular season. Neither Utah nor BYU has won a Big 12 title. BYU lost in the championship game last year to Texas Tech, which became the league’s lone playoff representative. A Morning Holy War? No Problem The Utes and Cougars will kick off at 10 a.m. local time at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City to accommodate a noon time slot for television on the East Coast. "Early, 10 a.m.," Utah coach Morgan Scalley said. "But I know our fans are juiced and fired up and they’ll be there early and excited for this one." BYU coach Kalani Sitake tried to play nice about having to roll out of bed for the early start. "It’s a little bit different," he said, adding there’s no doubt his players will be ready. "The guys are really focused. There’s more energy and more effort towards the preparation for this game than ever before." BYU has won three straight in the series that Utah dominated with nine consecutive wins before that. Utah quarterback Devon Dampier said he couldn’t go anywhere the entire offseason without hearing about the rivalry. "I understand what this means to the state, for sure," he said. A Football Junkie's Dream Week Texas Tech coach Joey McGuire plans to pay attention to his television set, first when the initial playoff rankings come out Tuesday night, then on other games that will have playoff implications. The Red Raiders host West Virginia on Saturday night. "Yeah, I’ll be tuned in. It’s going to be really interesting," McGuire said. "And then it’s going be really interesting, like, as a college football fan and then a guy that’s tracking everything right now. This weekend is huge for a lot of football teams." The Big 12 is the only Power 4 conference never to have multiple teams in the playoff. McGuire expects the Red Raiders to start out in the initial playoff ranking around where they are in the AP Top 25 poll, "which is good — striking distance," he said Monday. They'll need to finish in the top 11 because the 12th spot will go to the highest-ranked Group of Six team, which currently is No. 20 Boise State. He points to SEC matchups including No. 2 Georgia at No. 12 Mississippi, and No. 9 Alabama at No. 15 LSU. Then there's No. 11 Ohio State, minus quarterback Julian Sayin, hosting Oregon and top-ranked Miami traveling to No. 4 Notre Dame. McGuire said this week "is probably as big of a Saturday as we’ve seen in college football in a long time." Utah can count on a high ranking as one of three remaining unbeaten teams along with Miami and No. 5 UCLA. Scalley went into a two-minute explanation promising that his team won't get caught up in the CFP hype. "I’m pretty confident in our guys that they’re not going to look beyond this week," he said. Old Friends Are Now Opposing Coaches Scalley and Sitake are coaching at their alma maters and several members of their staffs coached or played at the other school. Sitake was a fullback under BYU coach Lavelle Edwards. Scalley was a safety and punt returner for the Utes. They worked together on the staff of Utah coach Kyle Whittingham when Sitake was the defensive coordinator and Scalley the safeties coach. Sitake left in 2015 to become defensive coordinator at Oregon State, then was named BYU’s coach in 2016. Scalley became Utah's defensive coordinator in 2016 and replaced Whittingham, who stepped down last December after compiling a school-record 177 wins, then was hired two weeks later at Michigan. Scalley and Sitake are close friends. Before the season they had dinner together along with Utah State coach Bronco Mendenhall, a former BYU coach. Scalley said Sitake is "the ultimate competitor. Respect him so much as a human for the good that he does, the good that he is." Sitake recalled that he and Scalley believed during their time at Utah that they could be head coaches someday, "but I don’t know if we saw this happening where he’s coaching his alma mater and I’m with my alma mater." After Earlier Stumbles, A Challenging November Awaits Two weeks ago, Texas Tech, BYU and Utah all were 6-0. BYU lost at UCF in double overtime the same day that Texas Tech fell on the road at Cincinnati. Texas Tech rebounded to beat No. 24 Arizona last Saturday while BYU beat Arizona State. Utah has won 14 straight, the longest active streak in the FBS. The Utes' schedule is considerably tougher over the final month of the season after outscoring their first eight opponents 311-127, including last week's lopsided win at Cincinnati. Utah also plays at Arizona and TCU, then finishes the regular season at home against West Virginia. BYU has games remaining against Baylor and Cincinnati sandwiched around a road contest at Kansas. Texas Tech has road games at Oklahoma State and Baylor, then hosts TCU to finish the regular season. The four teams tied for third place with two league losses, Arizona, Baylor, No. 17 Houston and Oklahoma State, haven't been mathematically eliminated but need collapses by the teams above them. articles.title: Herd Hierarchy: Are The Bears The NFL’s Best Team? Seahawks, Chiefs Slide
articles.summary: Cowherd revealed his latest Herd Hierarchy, featuring a new team at No. 1 after the defending champion Seahawks, last week’s top team, fell to 4-4.
articles.body: Colin Cowherd predicted the Chicago Bears and Seattle Seahawks would meet in the NFC title game, and after Monday night’s 34-17 Chicago win, he thinks the Bears are the best team in football. Cowherd revealed his latest Herd Hierarchy, featuring a new team at No. 1 after the defending champion Seahawks, last week’s top team, fell to 4-4. Here are Cowherd’s Week 8 Herd Hierarchy rankings: 10. Kansas City ChiefsRecord: 5-2Previous ranking: 5 ↓ Cowherd’s thoughts: "Kansas City is still good, but they’ve got to clean up the penalties, they’ve got to clean up the kicking game. Back-to-back losses to Seattle and Denver, they’re going to go 8-2 because the next three games are a layup before they have to go to Buffalo in a short week. "They have the worst penalty differential in the league. They need a No. 2 wide receiver. I think they’re fine, they’ve got a great coach, great DC. Travis Kelce, 37, I prefer he not be the No. 1 target on big plays. I think they’re just kind of unraveling in a few spots … I think they’ll clean it up and be a top-five team by Thanksgiving." 9. Detroit LionsRecord: 5-2Previous ranking: 7 ↓ Cowherd’s thoughts: "They’re playing better defense! Jack Campbell, though — cross your fingers. Great player, great human. He’s going to be out, and that doesn’t help. "They’ve outgained opponents in five straight games. They are very reliant on the health of their O-line, because Jared Goff can be a sitting duck if he doesn’t have time. I never really trust their defense in a big spot — maybe I have them low, I have them No. 9." 8. Los Angeles RamsRecord: 4-4Previous ranking: 9 ↑ Cowherd’s thoughts: "I’d take the Rams to beat the Lions if they played on a neutral field, because I just think if Davante Adams is healthy they have a great offense, too. It is remarkable how much they depend on him, even with Puka Nacua, all the tight ends, Matthew Stafford and Sean McVay. "When Davante Adams doesn’t play, 26th-ranked passing offense. So, Myles Garrett is coming back, only team in the top five in offense and defense. They’re an uneven team, they’re yet to play four quarters of great football … they’ve got to cinch that up." 7. Jacksonville JaguarsRecord: 5-2Previous ranking: Unranked ↑ Cowherd’s thoughts: "People think I have the Jags low. It’s the division. What am I supposed to do when you play the Titans twice a year and the Colts twice a year? And I don’t even know if I like the Texans now. … Liam Coen is the best coach in the league nobody talks about. If that guy was coaching in L.A. or New York or Chicago, he would be the talk of the league. "They do a lot well, but it’s a bad division. I probably should have them at six or five, I’ve got them at seven. I will say: Travis Hunter, Parker Washington, those are two of the top five athletes in the NFL." 6. New England PatriotsRecord: 5-3Previous ranking: 4 ↓ Cowherd’s thoughts: "The Patriots are beat up. I think it’s the most underrated team in the league. They were missing their No. 1 receiver, their No. 2 receiver, their No. 3 receiver, their No. 2 back, their No. 1 tight end: Drake Maye put the franchise on his shoulders in the second half. And I think they’re really good — five straight games with multiple touchdown passes, and they haven’t had a lot of their weapons. "They got the Packers, Lions and Bills coming, I think they could sweep those teams. … Drake Maye, I’ll take the over on one Lombardi Trophy. They just got to get healthier." 5. Buffalo BillsRecord: 6-1Previous ranking: 6 ↑ Cowherd’s thoughts: "By an inch, Buffalo. No. 1 scoring offense. Multiple giveaways in four of their last five games. That’s why I keep them here. You can’t do it. You just can’t do it. It’s like the Chiefs and penalties. I love a lot! You can’t give me ‘worst penalty differential,’ that’s starting to sound like stuff the Cowboys do. "Too many giveaways for this team, and they are bad on the back end. Which means you can outplay a team and then lose. It’s like a bad bullpen in baseball. Can’t have it." 4. Seattle SeahawksRecord: 4-4Previous ranking: 1 ↓ Cowherd’s thoughts: "Seattle’s fine. Like Kansas City, it’d be nice if they had another receiver in the building. But Monday night they’re playing musical chairs with the offensive line — they don’t have their left tackle, left guard or right guard. That’s not going to work with Jeffery Simmons and Montez Sweat, who are game wreckers. "It was the first game back for their running back, it was their third-straight primetime game. … Seattle’s got too many good players, too good of a coach, too much talent … last night was a bad spot, I still think they are a top-four team." 3. Denver BroncosRecord: 6-2Previous ranking: 8 ↑ Cowherd’s thoughts: "I’ve given up trying to figure out Denver. Fifteen straight one-possession wins. I don’t get it. I don’t get how you can be bad in every first half offensively. I love their personnel. In fact, if you need a wide receiver, call them. They got guys like Marvin Mims Jr. they don’t throw to. "I love their talent, and there is something that QB Bo Nix unlocks late in games. They’re 5-0 in one-score games. But they’ve been outgained by almost 700 yards. They do things historically that make no sense, but roster, head coach, playmakers, pass rush … I can’t deny it." 2. San Francisco 49ersRecord: 6-1Previous ranking: 2 Cowherd’s thoughts: "They’re going to get healthier now. Nick Bosa, Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel coming back. Look at their schedule, they’re going to start stockpiling wins. "Three of their six wins this season have come against the Seahawks, Broncos and Rams. Really well-coached, really good team — fewest big plays allowed, so they make you march down the field on them." 1. Chicago BearsRecord: 6-2Previous ranking: 3 ↑ Cowherd’s thoughts: "What do you want me to say? I mean, Jeffery Simmons and Montez Sweat, their big weakness was ‘well, the back-end.’ Well, now they’re not blitzing. Lowest blitz rate of the season, and yet they pressured Sam Darnold 12 times and sacked him three — should have been six. "And oh, by the way, they’re getting back their high-priced safety in December, Malik Muhammad their corner cover is coming back in a couple of weeks. So the safety and the corner positions, viewed as weaknesses, are going to be empowered and emboldened here in the next month and a half." FOX SPORTS NEWSLETTERYour teams. Your sports. articles.title: Ohio State Must Find A Way To Support Freshman Luke Fahey
articles.summary: Ohio State can't put everything on freshman QB Luke Fahey. Brady Quinn explains why the Buckeyes must make key offensive adjustments to get their season back on track.
articles.body: Ohio State is suddenly staring at a stretch of unfamiliar territory — one that hasn't been seen in Columbus since the fallout of "Tattoogate." Following the Buckeyes' second regular-season loss of the season, a defeat at the hands of USC last week, Ryan Day's program has now dropped four of its last 10 games. Credit Lincoln Riley and the Trojans. Their backs were against the wall, and when there was a play to be made, USC seized the opportunity. The last time Ohio State went 6-4 over a 10-game stretch was in 2011, when the program was navigating the fallout from Jim Tressel's resignation. Led by interim head coach Luke Fickell, the Buckeyes finished 6-7 before ushering in a new era under my colleague, Urban Meyer. Meyer quickly restored Ohio State to national prominence, delivering a national championship and an undefeated record against "that team up North." Ohio State's Problems Go Beyond Luke Fahey This season is far from over for Ohio State. But if the Buckeyes hope to get back into the College Football Playoff conversation, they'll need to adapt their offense to support true freshman quarterback Luke Fahey. If you looked only at the box score from Ohio State's loss to USC, you might wonder how the Buckeyes dominated nearly every statistical category yet still lost by two scores. But there was one area where they fell short — and it's one that I believe often gets overlooked: red-zone touchdown percentage. The difference between settling for a field goal and punching it into the end zone can have a significant impact over the course of a game. Those missed opportunities can ultimately be the difference between a win and a loss. Ohio State reached the red zone four times against USC but came away with just one touchdown and 12 total points. But wait, it gets worse. Ohio State had 11 offensive drives in the game, eight of which reached USC territory and into what we call the "fringe." That included drives that reached the USC 21-yard line (ending in a field goal), the 31 (ending in a fumble), the 22 (ending in a field goal) and the 36 (ending in a punt after a negative run and a five-yard penalty). The part of the field where you aren't in the red zone, but are in field goal range, is an area most offensive coordinators often look to take shots at the end zone. Red Zone defense changes for most defensive coordinators. Defenses can play more two-high, middle-of-the-field-open (MOFO) coverages (Cover 2, Cover 4 and variations of quarter-quarter-half) while still allowing defenders to also play more aggressively against the run without worrying as much about giving up a deep ball over their heads. That approach also makes it more difficult to isolate a star receiver like Jeremiah Smith. Defenses can dedicate two defenders to him while still keeping enough support in the box to defend the run. This is where Ohio State's offense struggled most. From USC's 40-yard line and in, Fahey completed just 7 of 20 passes, including a ball that should have been intercepted. He also took a costly sack on a play where he initially appeared to evade the rush, only to slow down and get caught from behind. The numbers become even more concerning when factoring in pressure. Fahey completed just three passes under duress in this critical area of the field. The reality is, this is the most challenging area of the field for an inexperienced quarterback. Passing windows shrink, demanding greater precision and accuracy. Decision-making becomes paramount, too. The quarterback has less time to process what the defense is showing him, and when you are pressured, that time is even more scarce. I experienced this in my first start at Notre Dame back in 2003. We were facing a Top 25-ranked Purdue team in West Lafayette. Little did I know that I'd attempt 59 passes that day, the second-most in Notre Dame history behind Terry Hanratty, who threw 63 times in a 1967 loss to, you guessed it, Purdue. We fell behind early, failed to establish a running game and finished with just 25 yards from our backfield. That put us in desperation mode, forcing the football downfield and ultimately resulting in four interceptions. To add insult to injury, I was probably hit 15 or 16 times that afternoon by Shaun Phillips and Ray Edwards. We also ran a wide receiver slip screen several times. Our play-side tackle would bluff the defensive end before releasing downfield to block for the receiver. That left Phillips with a free run at me, and he made sure to punish me for not blocking him. At one point, he told me, "I'm going to be here all day." And he wasn't wrong. In the end, there were enough positives — including an 85-yard touchdown pass to Maurice Stovall on a sight adjustment against a Will-Weak safety blitz just before halftime — for my coaching staff and teammates to believe in me. They gave me the opportunity to work through the growing pains and develop into the player I would eventually become. Unfortunately for Fahey, he's playing in an era that lacks patience and there is no room for development. I'm sure Fahey would like to have a few plays back, but the loss wasn't all on him. He was a true freshman making his first career start on the road. Pundits enjoy brining up Ohio State's 2014 national championship team as evidence that the Buckeyes can win it all with a backup quarterback. But that team was built differently. This is a program that has sent six wide receivers to the NFL in the first round since 2022. The Buckeyes have also ranked among the Big Ten's best passing offenses during that span. Ohio State has built its offensive identity around getting the football into the hands of its playmakers, allowing them to create explosive plays and put points on the board. The quarterback's ability to operate the offense at a high level is at a premium. This is one reason why I'd love to see Ohio State spread the field more often. There's a misconception among some playcallers that empty formations automatically put more pressure on the quarterback. Yes, you are more vulnerable in pass protection. However, it creates additional space for receivers and makes it more difficult for defenses to double-team a specific player. Empty formations also force defenses to show their hand. Are they playing man or zone coverage? If it's zone, what type? Are they bringing pressure or dropping into coverage? You can find all of these answers in empty formations displacing a running back or tight end out wide and watching their alignment. Ohio State ran just three empty-formation plays against USC. On the one completion Fahey did have, Smith might have hit his head on the goalpost if he didn't bobble the ball on his way to the ground for a 12-yard gain. The Buckeyes have no room for error or time to lick their wounds. They'll likely need to win out to keep their hopes of playing for a Big Ten championship alive. Standing in their way is an Oregon defense that has improved considerably over the past four weeks and still has an outside shot at reaching the conference title game itself. One Name To Know … Gio Lopez, Wake Forest The college basketball season has tipped off (great win for my Irish in Rome!), and it's reminded me of the great blue bloods from my childhood: Kentucky, UCLA, Indiana, Wake Forest and Arizona. It's ironic that the football success of these programs has been inconsistent at best — until recently. All five are now ranked in the AP Top 25, with Indiana entering the season as the defending national champions. What's particularly interesting to me is how the roster-building strategies that have shaped college basketball for years are now playing out in college football. Since the one-and-done rule went into effect, elite basketball programs have learned to recruit, develop and retain five-star talent in an environment where players are increasingly focused on maximizing their market value and NBA Draft stock. These blue-blood basketball programs, whose athletic departments have spent years navigating this evolving landscape, have adapted to a new world in college football— one in which roster building and retention are critical to your success. One of the best examples is Wake Forest head coach Jake Dickert, now in his second season with the Demon Deacons. Dickert left Washington State for the opportunity to lead a Power Four program, and he's off to a strong start. After guiding Wake Forest to a 9-4 record and a bowl victory in 2025, Dickert has positioned the Demon Deacons to compete for an ACC title and potentially earn a College Football Playoff berth. A big reason for that success is quarterback Gio Lopez. The Demon Deacons' junior signal-caller began his career at South Alabama, where he became a full-time starter in 2024 after seeing limited action as a freshman. Lopez played well enough to catch the attention of perhaps the greatest football coach of all time, Bill Belichick, earning him an opportunity at North Carolina. After a disappointing season in Chapel Hill, Lopez found a home not too far down Tobacco Road in Winston-Salem. On film, Lopez reminds me of a point guard in the way he operates the offense. The left-hander is crafty, distributing the ball all over the field. He moves effortlessly in and out of the pocket and has enough arm strength to make throws from the far hash to the sideline. Lopez has accounted for 24 total touchdowns this season while throwing just one interception. Lopez's improvement has been steady throughout the season, and his numbers against pressure are a reflection of that growth. According to PFF, Lopez ranks fifth among Power Four quarterbacks in passer rating when facing pressure. He'll have an opportunity to build on those numbers this week against FCS opponent Merrimack. Keep an eye on the Demon Deacons down the stretch. They travel to SMU and Georgia Tech before closing out the regular season on Thanksgiving against fellow Tobacco Road resident Duke. If Wake Forest wins out, it could set the stage for a rematch with Miami in the ACC Championship Game. Even with a loss, an 11-2 record — with both defeats coming against the current No. 1 team in the country — could be enough to earn the Demon Deacons a spot in the College Football Playoff. What I'm Watching … Miami (FL) at Notre Dame I’ve always felt "Catholics vs. Convicts" was offensive. I mean … not all students who attend Notre Dame are Catholic. On a more serious note: How could you not be excited for the best game of the college football season? This matchup has plenty of similarities to the 1988 classic, when No. 1 Miami — riding a 36-game regular-season winning streak — traveled to South Bend to take on the No. 4 Fighting Irish. The game lived up to the hype, as Miami quarterback Steve Walsh connected with Andre Brown on fourth down to bring the Hurricanes within one point. Head coach Jimmy Johnson elected to go for two, but Notre Dame safety Pat Terrell batted down Walsh’s pass to seal the victory for the Irish. Notre Dame would go on to claim the national championship after defeating West Virginia in the Fiesta Bowl. That game featured no shortage of star power, much like this week's matchup, which will be headlined by the two teams' starting quarterbacks. Their paths to their respective programs, however, couldn't be more different — a reflection of this era of college football. Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr is a throwback. Despite having ties to Michigan, he committed to the Irish early in the recruiting process and never wavered. A four-star recruit, Carr enrolled early, redshirted his first season and even helped Notre Dame build its recruiting class. Now, he enters this matchup as a potential first-round NFL Draft pick with eligibility remaining. Given the season he's having, it's hard to imagine him not being among the first names called in the 2027 NFL Draft. This could be his signature win as Notre Dame's quarterback and propel him to the top of the Heisman race, where he's currently listed at +750. On the other side is Miami quarterback Darian Mensah, who is emblematic of today's college football landscape. Now at his third school, Mensah followed a promising start at Tulane with a record-setting season at Duke. After leading the Blue Devils to an ACC championship and a Sun Bowl victory, where he was named MVP, Mensah attracted the attention of Miami — and the highest bidder in the Sunshine State. What's been most impressive about Mensah is how quickly Miami has seen a return on its investment. In his first season working with offensive coordinator Shannon Dawson, Mensah is tied for the national lead with 25 touchdown passes while leading the country in passer rating. He's been everything Miami hoped he would be, but this matchup represents his biggest remaining test of the regular season — and perhaps his best opportunity to deliver a Heisman moment. He's currently listed at +160 to win the award. The X-factor will be Mensah’s No. 1 target: Miami wide Malachi Toney, aka "Baby Jesus," who plays by the motto of G.A.B.O.S — Game Ain’t Based On Sympathy. His ability to separate in and out of cuts is rare, and he's making a case as the best wide receiver in college football (yes, that includes Jeremiah Smith). Toney is currently listed at +410 to win the Heisman Trophy, and his dazzling catches could allow him to steal the show if Notre Dame's defense can't find a way to limit his impact. Last season, Toney caught six passes for 82 yards and a touchdown in Miami's season-opening win over the Irish. Toney and Mensah have an even stronger connection, which could spell trouble for a Notre Dame defense already dealing with significant absences. Starting cornerback DJ McKinney, safety Brauntae Johnson and linebacker Drayk Bowen — who wears the green dot for the defense — are out for this matchup. This should be another classic in South Bend! articles.title: Raphinha 'devora' a Rivaldo, Lewandowski... y viene a por Luis Suárez
articles.standfirst: Su doblete contra el Aston Villa le convirtió en el tercer máximo goleador del Barcelona en Champions
articles.summary: Su doblete contra el Aston Villa le convirtió en el tercer máximo goleador del Barcelona en Champions
articles.body: Raphinha ni siquiera estuvo entre los 30 candidatos al Balón de Oro 2026 después de una temporada en la que las lesiones condicionaron buena parte de su rendimiento. El brasileño, sin embargo, ha vuelto a encontrar la regularidad y atraviesa un momento extraordinario. A estas alturas del curso, se ha convertido en uno de los futbolistas más en forma del planeta... y sus números empiezan a estar a la altura de algunas de las grandes leyendas que han pasado por el Barcelona. El mes de noviembre acaba de echar a rodar y Raphinha, reconvertido por Hansi Flick en delantero centro, ya ha superado sus registros goleadores de la pasada temporada. En apenas 13 partidos suma 19 tantos entre todas las competiciones. Los dos últimos llegaron frente al Aston Villa en Champions y le permitieron superar a Rivaldo y Lewandowski para convertirse en el tercer máximo goleador del Barcelona en la historia de la competición. Los 125 tantos de Leo Messi son inalcanzables, pero el brasileño ya tiene a tiro los 25 de Luis Suárez: está a solo tres de igualar al uruguayo. Su extraordinario momento también se refleja en la clasificación de máximos goleadores de esta edición de la Champions. Raphinha suma cuatro tantos en las cuatro primeras jornadas y comparte el liderato de la tabla. Bwin le coloca entre los principales candidatos a terminar como máximo artillero del torneo, con una cuota de 7.0. Por delante aparecen Kylian Mbappé, Harry Kane y Erling Haaland, todos ellos con una cotización de 6.0. Las apuestas deportivas también empiezan a reconocer el impacto de un futbolista que ha pasado de convivir con las dudas físicas a convertirse en una de las grandes amenazas ofensivas de Europa. De los goles de Raphinha dependerán buena parte de las opciones del Barcelona de volver a levantar una Champions que se le resiste desde 2015. El doblete ante el Aston Villa permitió a los azulgranas reaccionar después de la derrota frente al PSG y recuperar sensaciones en el momento adecuado. Llegados al ecuador de la fase liga, el conjunto de Flick tiene bien encarrilada su clasificación directa para los octavos de final y vuelve a mirar hacia las rondas decisivas con ambición. El brasileño quiere ser uno de los grandes protagonistas de ese camino. Bwin mantiene al Barcelona entre los principales favoritos para conquistar el título, con una cuota de 4.5... sólo superada por el PSG (4.3). Las mejores casas de apuestas reflejan así la exigencia de una carrera en la que los azulgranas tendrán que competir con algunos de los grandes aspirantes europeos. Raphinha, mientras tanto, sigue haciendo historia: ya ha dejado atrás a Rivaldo y Lewandowski... y tiene entre ceja y ceja alcanzar a Luis Suárez. Si mantiene este ritmo, su nombre puede terminar ocupando un lugar todavía más destacado en la historia del club.

articles.title: PV Sindhu sees new wave in Indian badminton: 'Initially, there was a gap, but now we have these girls'
articles.summary: PV Sindhu has spent much of her career carrying India's challenge in women's singles badminton.
articles.body: PV Sindhu has spent much of her career carrying India's challenge in women's singles badminton. Now, as the 31-year-old returns to the world's top six, she is seeing a group of younger Indian shuttlers begin to make their mark on the international circuit.Tanvi Sharma, Anmol Kharb, Unnati Hooda, Devika Sihag and Ashmita Chaliha have all had notable results in 2026. Sindhu is pleased to see more Indian names competing at this level."I am really happy to see so many youngsters doing well. Ashmita has done really well, Anmol has been doing really well, and of course, there are Unnati and Tanvi," Sindhu said during a virtual media interaction on Wednesday."We are seeing a lot of youngsters, and I am really happy that there are four or five girls coming up, doing well and representing the country. It is always nice to have your fellow athletes and youngsters coming up, doing well and representing the country. What else do we need?"Sindhu also recalled a period when the next generation in women's singles was difficult to identify."Initially, there was a gap, and we did not know who the juniors coming through would be. But now I can say that there are these girls who are doing really well in the women's circuit. I am happy to see so many youngsters doing well," she added.The results this season give an indication of the depth Sindhu is referring to. Tanvi, 17, became the youngest champion in Taipei Open history in August, beating Vietnam's Nguyen Thuy Linh 21-16, 21-16 in the final. It was India's first women's singles title at the tournament since Saina Nehwal won it in 2008.Ashmita won her maiden BWF World Tour title at the Korea Masters, coming back from a game down to beat China's Han Qianxi 14-21, 21-14, 21-14. The 27-year-old from Assam then beat former world champion Akane Yamaguchi 21-19, 21-18 at the French Open to reach her first Super 750 quarterfinal.Unnati, who has climbed to a career-best World No. 19, reached the women's singles quarterfinals at the Asian Games. She took a game off Yamaguchi before going down 16-21, 21-14, 17-21.Anmol won the Turkiye International Challenge in October and followed it with a semifinal appearance at the HYLO Open. She beat Unnati in three games in the quarterfinals before losing to Sindhu 13-21, 16-21.Sihag had opened India's BWF World Tour title account for the year by winning the Thailand Masters Super 300 in February.HYLO Open title takes Sindhu back to World No. 6The younger players have been making progress while Sindhu has put together one of her stronger seasons in recent years. Her HYLO Open victory was her second BWF World Tour title of 2026, following her Japan Open triumph in July. She had also reached the French Open final the previous week, where she lost to World No. 1 An Se-young.In Germany, Sindhu beat Denmark's Line Højmark Kjærsfeldt 21-12, 21-14 in 39 minutes. She completed the campaign without dropping a game. The title took her back to World No. 6, a ranking she had last held in 2022."Touchwood, I am happy that I am back again. After 2022, I am back in the top six, if I am not wrong. I am happy that things are going well," she said.Sindhu, though, believes there is still considerable room to improve. "I would say there is a lot more room, a lot more space for improvement and I am getting there. I am happy with this, and I think definitely there are a lot of things to work on. There is a lot more space to improve. I am really looking forward to that," she added.The former world champion is confident she can return to the level she reached during her most successful years. Sindhu won the World Championship in 2019 and has two Olympic medals."If you take care of your body, definitely yes. The answer is yes. There are a lot of athletes playing in their 30s, at 31 or 32, and there have been a lot of athletes who were at their top. So why not get back there at the top again?" she said."I am getting there, and I am there. I am saying this because I know that I can still do it. That is why I said there is a lot of space, a lot of room to improve."'31 is the new 21': Sindhu on managing her bodySindhu's recent run has come with a more selective approach to her tournament schedule. Her support team includes strength and conditioning coach Wayne Lombard, her physiotherapist and coach Irwansyah Adi Pratama. The group assesses her condition regularly before deciding on training loads and tournament participation."More than anything, we make sure we smartly take decisions about which tournaments are to be played and how the body condition is. Am I feeling good or am I feeling my 100 per cent? Every single day, we analyse it accordingly," she said."At times, you make sure you change the schedule or work accordingly, depending on my body condition. That way, it has really been working out. With my experience, I do tell them how I feel and accordingly we work on that."Sindhu's decision to skip the Korea Open and subsequent tournaments after a long stretch of competition was part of that plan. She wanted time to return home, recover and prepare before getting back on court."The initial plan was that I would be playing other tournaments as well. But I think it was important for me to take this decision because I needed to take care of my body and get back stronger on court again," she said.But she is clear that playing week after week without being fully fit is not an option."You are not 20 anymore and you cannot keep playing tournaments back-to-back. You need to make sure that whatever tournaments you play, you give your 100 per cent. To give that 100 per cent, you have to make sure you are physically and mentally at your best," she said."If you are at 50 per cent, you make sure you step back, recover, come back stronger and bounce back stronger. Accordingly, you work on your mistakes and your game."If you are not at 100 per cent and go at 50 per cent, that is not how it is going to be. You would lose a lot more confidence because you cannot give your 100 per cent. Losing to some unknown player when you are not at your 100 per cent can make you feel really low, and you might not get that confidence back," she said.An Se-young challenge and badminton's 15-point formatSindhu's French Open final against An Se-young gave her plenty to review. She won the opening game but could not hold on to the advantage, eventually losing the match. That extended the South Korean’s dominance over the Indian to 11-0."After taking that first game, I just felt that in the second game I gave her a huge lead. By the time I covered it, it was almost too late," she said."In the third game, I was there, I was leading by two or three points, and I should have gone with the same tempo. I felt that I could have played the right stroke at the right time. I gave her two or three points easily. I made some unforced errors, which is what I felt."Sindhu expects to make changes before their next meeting."I am definitely very certain that in the coming days or coming months, there will be some changes in making sure it will be difficult for her," she said.The demands of women's singles also have changed over the years, Sindhu said, with rallies getting longer and patience becoming increasingly important."Badminton as a sport has been changing every single time. Back then, it was more about attacking play, but now there are longer rallies and you have to stay more patient on court," she said.The switch to a 15-point scoring format from next year will require another adjustment. Sindhu believes players will have less time to recover from a slow start."We have been playing 21 for so many years now. It is important that we make sure we train and practise that scoring system as well," she said."In 21 points, there was still time. Even if five points had gone, people could come back. But now, once those five or six points go, half the game is over. It is important that you are alert from the beginning," she said."You cannot give away easy points because by the time you realise it, half the game is over. You have to be on your feet every single time."Having secured her place in the season-ending BWF World Tour Finals, Sindhu will now turn her attention to the tournament as she looks to finish the season on a strong note.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "Un honor luchar juntos": la emotiva despedida de los compañeros de Selección a David Ospina
articles.standfirst: James Rodríguez, Falcao y Cuadrado reaccionan al retiro de David Ospina de la Selección Colombia
articles.summary: James Rodríguez, Falcao y Cuadrado reaccionan al retiro de David Ospina de la Selección Colombia
articles.body: El fútbol colombiano se vistió de nostalgia tras el anuncio oficial del retiro de David Ospina del fútbol profesional. El histórico arquero antioqueño, considerado uno de los referentes más grandes de la historia de la Selección Colombia, puso fin a una carrera de más de dos décadas defendiendo el arco Tricolor en torneos orbitales y grandes ligas del mundo. La noticia desató una inmediata lluvia de mensajes y reacciones en las redes sociales por parte de sus compañeros de generación, aquellos con los que compartió batallas épicas, mundiales y momentos imborrables para el deporte nacional. Uno de los primeros en reaccionar fue James Rodríguez, con quien además de compartir una estrecha relación personal y familiar, lideró la época dorada de la Selección Colombia en las Copas del Mundo (Brasil 2014, Rusia 2018 y la cita orbital de 2026). "¡Eres un grande, el número 1! Gracias por las alegrías y por tu carrera que ha sido ejemplar. Orgulloso de conocer ese gran ser humano, me siento un privilegiado de poderte decir hermano. ¡Hemos luchado juntos, reído juntos, llorado juntos en muchas batallas! Te deseo lo mejor en esta nueva etapa de tu vida. Te quiero", expresó James a través de sus redes sociales. Las muestras de cariño y respeto hacia el guardameta no pararon allí. Históricos como Juan Guillermo Cuadrado y Radamel Falcao García también dedicaron palabras de profundo reconocimiento al legado de Ospina. Juan Guillermo Cuadrado: "¡Excelente, mi capi y líder! Un honor haber compartido tantas batallas juntos. Hiciste historia. Bendiciones para lo que viene", destacó el volante sobre los años compartidos vistiendo la camiseta nacional. Radamel Falcao García: El 'Tigre' también se manifestó con un caluroso mensaje: "Querido amigo, ha sido un honor compartir contigo parte de este viaje... Te deseo lo mejor en lo que viene para tu vida. ¡Abrazo grande!", rubricando la hermandad tejida en la Tricolor. David Ospina se marcha tras 21 años de carrera profesional impecable, donde dejó una huella imborrable en el corazón de los hinchas y de las nuevas generaciones del fútbol colombiano. Futbolistas actuales como Luis Díaz y el guardameta Camilo Vargas también ponderaron su calidad humana y su ejemplo bajo los tres palos: Luis Díaz: "Qué orgullo y privilegio haber compartido camerino contigo, hermano. Más allá del gran arquero, eres un ser humano increíble. Gracias por tanto, David. Siempre serás un ejemplo para todos". Camilo Vargas: "Existen jugadores que hacen historia, pero tú dejaste huella en cada corazón de las personas que te conocen". El propio Ospina se despedía de los terrenos de juego con una reflexión profunda sobre lo que significó su travesía por el deporte: "Al fútbol, le digo gracias... En mi pecho se quedan los escudos de mis batallas". El fútbol sudamericano despide a un auténtico gigante, pero su legado en la historia de la Selección Colombia permanecerá intacto para siempre.

articles.title: Joel Klatt’s 5 Takeaways From The 1st CFP Rankings: Is The Process Broken?
articles.summary: Joel Klatt has a problem with the College Football Playoff committee’s first top 25 of the season, and it has little to do with any one team.
articles.body: Joel Klatt has a problem with the College Football Playoff committee’s first top 25 of the season, and it has little to do with any one team. The committee unveiled its rankings Tuesday night, with Miami at No. 1, followed by Georgia, Utah and Indiana, and Ohio State at No. 12 as the first team out of the 12-team field. On the latest episode of "The Joel Klatt Show," Klatt said the process behind those rankings is the issue and pushed back on the idea that the first top 25 ranking doesn’t matter. Here are Joel Klatt's takeaways: 1.No Consistent Criteria Klatt’s thoughts: "They’re left to their own accord to rank teams based on any criteria they want. What you see generally — and we’ve seen this all the way back to 2014 when we started this exercise in the playoff era — is that you see certain criteria used at certain points and other criteria used at others. Record has an influence, obviously. Who you beat has an influence. Sometimes who you lost to, your strength of schedule — that’s been more of a common theme this year — your personnel, who’s injured, who’s not injured. "There’s all these different criteria, and none of them are valued over any other criteria. Well, that’s impossible. So, good people in that room, trustworthy people in that room, but that doesn’t make up for the fact that the process is broken." 2.13 Inputs Aren’t Enough Klatt’s thoughts: "What is one of the things that is broken in the process? The fact that there’s only 13 inputs, that there’s only 13 individuals that have an opinion on something that is so important in college football. In fact, the most important thing in college football. That’s wild. "We have to increase the number of inputs into this data set. That’s the process. That’s not their fault. They’re doing the best they can with the criteria that they’re given. They’re building a house with no blueprints." 3.This Top 25 Is An Outlier Klatt’s thoughts: "I know not everybody has a math background or a statistics background. … But we all kind of understand numbers, right? I mean, we have to balance our budgets. We've got to pay bills. We got to do all those things at home. So you kind of understand numbers, and you understand when something is an outlier. "You're going through your personal budget, and you know the month that you take a vacation, and you're like, 'well, our expenditures that month that's an outlier because we went on vacation,' and you understand that, so you don't base your entire yearly budget based on the amount of money you spent in the month that you went on vacation. "Well, I would argue that what they gave us on Tuesday night is about as big of an outlier as you can possibly get in a top 25. I don’t think that you could put 50 committees together and they would produce something that is this wild. "What do we do in statistics when we get a body of data? We throw out the edges and then evaluate the middle. It’s like a bell curve. Well, this top 25 is on the edge. It’s the very outskirts, and yet it’s the one that we’re going to use to represent all of college football and crown a champion." 4.Committee Is Killing Non-Conference Games Klatt’s thoughts: "The process of ranking teams this way, and having that process be the most meaningful thing in college football, is actively hurting the sport, and that’s the tough part. None of them are intending that, but that’s the truth. "Based on the top 25 that they gave us — and candidly, they have given us over the last two or three years, maybe even all the way back to 2014 in the playoff era — there is zero, and I mean zero reason to schedule a tough non-conference game. Seeing Texas and Ohio State play Week 2, Michigan and Oklahoma — these are great for the sport, and yet these games are dying. They are going extinct. And why? Because the committee is actively hunting them and shooting them out in the wild. There’s no other way to explain it, because they’re not valuing non-conference opponents." 5.The First Ranking Matters Klatt’s thoughts: "You heard a lot during the ranking show, ‘Slow down. This is only the beginning. Don’t overreact.’ No, these do matter, and they matter a great deal. In fact, the only ranking that is more important than the first ranking is the last one. "College football is a race. It’s a race to those 12 spots. And the top 25 that they gave us is the starting grid. We have NASCAR here on FOX. We have IndyCar here on FOX, and everybody qualifies, and the best cars get to start up front. They don’t have the burden of proof like the cars behind them. The cars behind them, they’ve got to pass them. If you ask any race car driver, would you rather start 12th or first, what do you think the answer is going to be? "Every game from this point forward has a value, and that value is attached to what they just gave us on Tuesday night." FOX SPORTS NEWSLETTERYour teams. Your sports. articles.title: An NFL Insider Just Put an Old Friend Back on the Bears’ Radar
articles.summary: Ryan Poles already addressed the biggest hole in the Bears’ defensive front. With the trade deadline approaching, his next move […]
articles.body:
Ryan Poles already addressed the biggest hole in the Bears' defensive front. With the trade deadline approaching, his next move could involve a player who helped Chicago's secondary last season.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport named Jets cornerback Nahshon Wright as someone to watch while discussing the Bears' remaining needs Tuesday. Wright earned a Pro Bowl selection in Chicago before leaving in free agency, but his time in New York has offered little opportunity to follow that performance.

That combination makes a potential reunion intriguing: the Bears could use another option at cornerback, and Wright wants a chance to play defense again.

"The other interesting one is Nahshon Wright," Rapoport mentioned. "He was with the Bears last year, is with the Jets now, is really not playing. Could that be a name to watch as well, just for some depth?"

Rapoport also said he did not believe Poles was finished making moves. His comments put Wright into the conversation without establishing that the teams are negotiating. There is no reported Bears offer or Jets asking price in that account. Still, the circumstances on both sides explain the connection.

Wright has appeared in three games for New York, playing 22 special-teams snaps without receiving a defensive snap. For someone coming off his most productive NFL season, that represents a considerable change.

ESPN's Rich Cimini reported that Wright was "definitely frustrated" about his lack of a defensive role. Asked whether he had requested a trade, Wright indicated he had not done so formally but had communicated his dissatisfaction. "I've expressed my feelings," Wright told Cimini .

That establishes his desire for a different opportunity. It does not establish that he has specifically asked to return to Chicago.

The Bears nevertheless know what he can provide in their defense. Wright appeared in all 17 games last season and started 16, recording five interceptions, 11 passes defended, two forced fumbles and three fumble recoveries. His production earned him his first Pro Bowl selection. Before arriving in Chicago, he had started only three games across four seasons with Dallas and Minnesota.

Dennis Allen's defense gave Wright an opportunity to show more than he had in his previous stops, accepting his flaws, while taking full advantage of his aggressive ball skills. If the Bears considered bringing him back, they would have firsthand knowledge of his strengths, limitations and preparation habits.

That familiarity could be useful when trying to incorporate a player during the season. Wright would still need to get current with Chicago's plans, but he would be returning to a coaching staff and defensive system he already knows.

Monday's victory in Seattle showed why the Bears might keep examining their options. Chicago's defense held the Seahawks to one conversion on 11 third downs. Jeffery Simmons immediately strengthened the pass rush, and the front helped make Sam Darnold uncomfortable throughout the night.

The secondary still had expensive mistakes. Tyrique Stevenson surrendered Jaxon Smith-Njigba's long touchdown before halftime, while defensive holding penalties wiped out two Montez Sweat sacks. Rookie cornerback Malik Muhammad missed the game with a toe injury.

An improved pass rush should help the coverage. Adding another outside corner could give Allen more choices when injuries or matchups test his depth. Wright's potential role would require consideration. His previous production would not automatically entitle him to a starting job, and the Bears would need to evaluate what he could offer now.

The acquisition cost would be equally important. After surrendering two first-round picks and a fourth-round selection in the Simmons trade, Chicago has reason to scrutinize every additional expenditure. A reunion would have to make sense at the Jets' price. That price, however, should not be significant, as Wright is a reserve that wants out.

For him, the immediate objective appears straightforward: getting back onto the field on defense. For the Bears, the question is whether a familiar player can strengthen a position that remains worth monitoring.

Rapoport has identified the possibility. With the Nov. 10 deadline approaching, Poles has another potential route to consider as he decides how much more this roster needs.

articles.title: Browns QB Watson enters concussion protocol after symptoms surfaced, Sanders could go against Saints
articles.summary: BEREA, Ohio (AP) — Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has been placed in the concussion protocol after experiencing symptoms Monday night.If Watson...
articles.body:
BEREA, Ohio (AP) — Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has been placed in the concussion protocol after experiencing symptoms Monday night.

If Watson is not cleared in time for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints, Shedeur Sanders would get his first start of the season.

Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit during the first quarter of last week's 27-6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers . The independent certified athletic trainer watching the game from the press box called down to the Browns sideline and Watson was given a gameday concussion evaluation and cleared by the unaffiliated neurotrauma consultant.

The 10-year veteran returned to the game and completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards, his second straight 300-yard game.

The Browns said Wednesday morning that Watson received evaluations after Sunday's game and Monday morning. He was cleared after showing no symptoms. Watson told the medical staff Tuesday morning he began experiencing symptoms Monday night when he was placed in the concussion protocol.

Sanders was in for four plays against the Steelers, and completed both of his passes for 2 yards. He started the final seven games of his rookie season last year, going 3-4 with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions.

articles.title: 3 Best MLB Free Agent Fits For Seiya Suzuki If He Leaves Cubs
articles.summary: Here are the three best MLB free agent fits for outfielder Seiya Suzuki if he leaves the Chicago Cubs.
articles.body: Power. Lots and lots of power. That's what one is getting if they sign Chicago Cubs right fielder and designated hitter Seiya Suzuki, who's arguably the biggest power threat on the MLB free agent market this winter. Plus, the 32-year-old Suzuki is coming off quite possibly the best all-around season of his MLB career, offering both a respectable defensive presence in right field and a potent threat from the right side of the plate. Here are the three best MLB free agent fits for Suzuki should he depart Chicago: Cincinnati Reds Simply put: The Cincinnati Reds need a right fielder. The Reds continue to struggle to get consistent production from their outfield and offense as a whole. Plus, the Eugenio Suárez reunion didn't live up to the hype in 2026, as he finished with a mere .212/.307/.433 slash line while splitting time at the hot corner and designated hitter, and is now a free agent. Suzuki would presumably become Cincinnati's starting right fielder, adding veteran assurance and an impactful veteran complement. Suzuki's electric bat would boost a Reds' offense that was last in MLB in hits (1,231) and on-base percentage (.305), 27th in runs (666) and 25th in slugging percentage (.394) last season. Prior to 2026, Suzuki was Chicago's primary designated hitter in 2025 before making 110 starts and 111 appearances altogether in right field last season. On that front, Suzuki posted a career-high 5.1 wins above replacement while also logging 14 defensive runs. Now, Cincinnati may want Héctor Rodríguez to be its everyday right fielder. In that case, Suzuki opens the season as the Reds' designated hitter and moves to right field if Rodríguez struggles or injury presents itself. While the Reds were fourth in the sport with 213 home runs last season, they need the offense, and Suzuki would provide a major lift in that regard. What could stop the Reds — who finished in last place in the National League Central with 75 wins last season — from making a push for Suzuki, though, is them potentially feeling they're not close enough to contending for the playoffs to be doling out a potential nine-figure contract. Rather, they may hope that Rodríguez emerges as a building block and be cost-effective in filling out the rest of their depth chart. Texas Rangers The Texas Rangers need some oomph, which is precisely what Suzuki would provide. Just one year ago in 2025, Suzuki, who boasts a career .472 slugging percentage and a 128 OPS+, totaled 32 home runs and 103 RBIs, both career highs. Suzuki would enhance a Texas offense that was just 25th in runs (673), 23rd in hits (1,296) and tied for 21st in slugging percentage (.396) last season. As for Suzuki's potential fit with the Rangers, designated hitter Joc Pederson is a free agent, which would be the easiest way to slide Suzuki into the mix. Concurrently, right fielder Brandon Nimmo has the versatility and experience playing all three outfield positions should Texas want to play Suzuki in right field. While Evan Carter is a commendable center fielder, he continues to struggle at the plate (Carter hit .194 across 455 plate appearances in 2026), creating a scenario where Texas could either move Wyatt Langford from left to center field or put Nimmo in center field, with Suzuki taking over in right field. Either way, the Rangers — who, aside from Langford, have been unable to get their touted young position players to progress as hitters — need more slugging, and they have the wiggle room to add to their outfield rotation. The Houston Astros won the American League West with a .500 record, edging out the Rangers by one game. It's reasonable to think the Rangers' starting rotation — a unit that led MLB with a 3.41 ERA in 2025 — will bounce back in 2027. With that in mind, a slightly improved offense could literally be all they need to win the AL West. All that said, Texas may prefer to retain Pederson, who hit 26 home runs and posted a .487 slugging percentage in 2026, on a short-term deal to be its designated hitter and avoid switching gears with who plays where in the outfield. Atlanta Braves At face value, the Atlanta Braves don't have a burning need for a right fielder. When putting a magnifying glass closer to the object at hand, though, signing Suzuki would be a slick move. For starters, the Braves were muzzled by the Los Angeles Dodgers — who were then swept by the Milwaukee Brewers in the NL Championship Series — in the NL Division Series, tallying just eight runs and 18 hits across the would-be four-game series. Meanwhile, versatile left fielder Mauricio Dubón, outfielder and midseason pickup Lane Thomas and designated hitter/first baseman Dominic Smith are free agents. Adding a considerable hitter who's also a body for the outfield mix would be timely. Suzuki represents a defensive alternative to Ronald Acuña Jr., who has underwhelmed at the corner outfield position by his standards of late and made 14 starts as the team's designated hitter last season, and offers a way for the Braves to ease the homegrown star into being the team's DH on a more consistent basis, if wanted. Plus, the combination of a torn ACL, as well as calf and hamstring issues, have limited Acuña to just 251 regular games since the outset of the 2023 MLB season. Adding another All-Star-caliber outfielder to the mix warrants consideration from a health standpoint, alone. Suzuki would fit Atlanta's timeline as an NL contender with a core of players who are primarily in their prime. articles.title: WWE Rumors on Jacob Fatu & AJ Styles, CM Punk Addresses John Cena Classic and Worlds Collide
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Jacob Fatu has been out of action for more than a month, but fans reportedly may not have to wait much longer to see him back on WWE programming.

According to PWInsider Elite (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News), Fatu's on-screen return is "not far off," as he has already filmed promotional material for a WarGames match at Survivor Series with his fellow Bloodline members.

On the Sept. 28 episode of Raw, Fatu was shockingly hit by a car in a parking garage. Jaida Parker was the driver, and after initially acting like it was an accident, she revealed herself to be a member of Royce Keys' 946 faction.

Fatu has been off television since then, but the rivalry between The Bloodline and 946 has continued to dominate Raw in recent weeks.

Carmelo Hayes and Cruz Montana have joined 946, giving them a numbers advantage over The Bloodline.

However, once Fatu returns, all the pieces will be in place for a five-on-five WarGames match pitting Roman Reigns, Fatu, Solo Sikoa, Jey Uso and Jimmy Uso against Keys, Hayes, Montana, Bronco Nima and Lucien Price.

While WWE has yet to announce the WarGames match, every indication is that The Bloodline vs. 946 is in the works, and Fatu returning would allow for the company to make it official.

There are times when WarGames matches feel thrown together and predicated on the calendar rather than a storyline that requires the stipulation, but that won't be the case for The Bloodline and 946, as their feud is tailor made for the double cage.

New information has emerged regarding WWE Hall of Famer AJ Styles' role at the WWE Performance Center.

On the heels of wrestling reporter Andrew Baydala (h/t WrestlePurists ) recently reporting that Styles has been "quietly running things" at the WWE PC for months, a new report suggests that isn't necessarily true.

According to Fightful Select (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News), a WWE PC source said Styles has not been "running things," although he recently "filled in to finish a class."

The source added that The Phenomenal One is a "constant and positive presence" at the PC, and they expect him to "continue to gain influence."

Since retiring from in-ring competition in January, Styles has continued working with WWE in a backstage capacity.

Last week, Cory Hays of False Finish reported that current NXT head Shawn Michaels is expected to replace Bruce Prichard as WWE's executive director of creative writing and talent when Prichard retires next year, at which point Styles will take on Michaels' role in NXT and at the WWE PC.

While that may prove to be the case, Fightful's report suggests Styles has not gotten to that point yet, as he is merely helping out at the PC rather than running the show.

CM Punk Announces Status for John Cena Classic, Worlds Collide

CM Punk confirmed Tuesday that he will be part of two upcoming WWE shows at the ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex in Orlando, Florida.

Commenting on a WWE Instagram post (h/t Mukherjee ) about the John Cena Classic on Dec. 14 and Worlds Collide on Dec. 15, Punk wrote, "I'm gonna work both shows."

During Monday night's episode of Raw, John Cena revealed additional details regarding the John Cena Classic, including its location. He also showed off the John Cena Classic Championship belt.

On top of that, Cena announced that Cody Rhodes is his first invitee to participate in the event.

Punk's post suggests he will wrestle a match as well in the John Cena Classic, which is being advertised as an opportunity for up-and-coming Superstars to prove themselves against established stars.

Along with the John Cena Classic, the co-branded WWE, NXT and AAA Worlds Collide was announced as part of WWE's takeover of the ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex.

Worlds Collide will be themed after the upcoming Marvel movie Avengers: Doomsday , which is set to release three days after the event.

articles.summary: WWE Hall of Famer The Undertaker has spent more than three decades as one of the most established and celebrated wrestlers of all time.
articles.body: WWE Hall of Famer The Undertaker has spent more than three decades as one of the most established and celebrated wrestlers of all time. His WWE contract has made him earn millions of dollars along the way. articles.title: How did Tiger Woods’ father shape his golf journey? Exploring Earl Woods’ influence, childhood training, military discipline and the family story behind his rise to golfing greatness
articles.summary: Explore how Earl Woods shaped Tiger Woods' golf journey through military discipline, unique training techniques, and emotional support from Kultida. Discover the family dynamics behind Tiger's rise to greatness.
articles.body: Tiger Woods’ ascent from child prodigy to one of the most powerful figures in the game was more than just natural ability. His father, Earl Woods, introduced him to the game of golf at a very young age and set up a training program that included technical instruction, mental conditioning and getting ready for pressure. Earl’s military background had a big impact on his coaching style, and he would often try his son’s concentration with strange distractions.Tiger’s dad didn’t raise him alone. Kultida Woods, Earl’s mother, counterbalanced his strictness with emotional guidance, discipline and encouragement. Their influence helped plant the seed for Tiger’s growth as a golfer and a competitor.How Tiger Woods’ father Earl Woods built his golfing foundationTiger’s father, Earl Woods, a retired US Army lieutenant colonel and former Green Beret, saw Tiger’s interest in golf when he was a baby. He started to introduce him to the game with simple activities, slowly turning early curiosity into structured practice.Earl is said to have put Tiger in a baby bouncer next to golf practice when he was about six months. By about 11 months, he had made a custom putter for his son. Tiger’s progress was staggering: purportedly he shot a 48 over nine holes at the age of three and won junior golf tournaments as a child.Earl taught the game in reverse, not beginning with the full golf swing. His focus was on putting, chipping and pitching before he moved on to the more complex elements of the sport. His coaching was not just about physical skills; he wanted Tiger to learn how to keep his head when the pressure was on.Earl’s military experience shaped his approach to preparing his mind. He would deliberately cause distractions when Tiger was practicing, making noises, coughing or jingling his keys as his son tried to hit a shot.It was to teach Tiger to concentrate in the face of interruption. Earl believed that competitive golf required the ability to tune out distractions, especially when distractions could come from the gallery, the opponents and the pressure of the tournament.He could be demanding, and some of his methods were criticized. But Tiger later confessed that his dad had prepared him for situations that others might find embarrassing or even painful. Earl wanted his son to build resilience, not rely on perfect playing conditions.How Kultida Woods balanced Earl’s strict training approachWhere Earl stressed discipline and competitive toughness, Kultida Woods provided guidance of another kind, and she helped keep the family emotionally balanced and encouraged Tiger to stay grounded as his success grew.She also encouraged Tiger's tradition of wearing red on Sundays, which became one of his most recognizable golfing signatures. Her influence balanced Earl’s hard-driving style of training and gave Tiger a combination of competitive discipline and emotional support.The family story behind Tiger Woods’ riseTiger was a family affair at its inception. Earl provided the technical and mental building blocks, and Kultida helped provide discipline and perspective. The influence of both together created the setting in which his golfing skills were formed.It was a big moment in the golfer-coach relationship as Tiger reportedly beat his father for the first time at the age of 11. By then, he already had an impressive junior record and experience playing against older players.Earl Woods’s influence never left Tiger as he developed and moved toward the professional game. It was an unconventional approach, but one that was designed to prepare his son for the demands of elite competition.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Players Championship 33: Luke Humphries beats Niels Zonneveld in final as Raymond van Barneveld closes in on world championship
articles.summary: World Grand Prix champion Luke Humphries continued his Leicester love affair to clinch his fourth Players Championship title of the campaign on Wednesday; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
Humphries has now prevailed in three of his four Players Championship appearances in Leicester this season, marking the perfect preparation for the upcoming Grand Slam of Darts admitted he was forced him to pull out of the European Championship last month and then struggling with huge weight loss and a lack of practice.

It was also a terrific day for Van Barneveld, who took a huge step towards world championship qualification with a run to his second ProTour quarter-final of 2026, while Gary Anderson moved him into the provisional Players Championship Finals field with a run to the last four.

"It was more about coming back and seeing what my energy levels are like because I've obviously been very ill for the last two weeks," admitted Humphries.

"I've had food poisoning and I've not really moved about a lot for three and a half weeks.

"I've lost a stone. Well I did when I went on the scales after eight or nine days. I weighed myself and I'd lost 15 pounds. Jesus, what the hell. I couldn't eat.

"I'd never miss a major if I could. I think that's the first one I've ever missed. I was devastated to miss the European Championship because I was on a good run after winning the Grand Prix.

"I didn't win the Swiss trophy but I played really good. So I thought to myself I feel like I'm a little bit back here and I can maybe go on and do something great this year and that's a backward step when you have to miss a tournament.

"I didn't practice for two weeks. I had a few throws the last four days. It re-evaluates that confidence again that makes you think you carried on from where you left off.

"To come here and win it takes you back a little bit. So obviously I know the game's there to win these things. But the way I've been the last few weeks it's an unexpected win for myself.

"I've had a good year. I still want to win another major. If it's not the Grand Slam or Players Championship, I want it to be the World Championship.

"I think that's the thing I really search for now. Put my name in the legacy of some of the greats that's ever been."

The world No 3 maintained his charge with back-to-back 6-2 victories against Steve Lennon and Gerwyn Price, before defying a 106.75 average from Anderson to triumph in an epic semi-final.

Humphries produced a brace of 12-dart breaks to seize the initiative against Zonneveld in the showpiece, before capping off a classy display with an 11-dart hold to triumph with a 103.77 average.

Henry Coates currently occupies the final provisional place at Minehead, having produced ton-plus averages in wins over James Wade and Mervyn King, only to succumb to Gerwyn Price in round three.

The 20-year-old has subsequently moved into the provisional world championship places at the expense of David Sharp, who was on the receiving end of a nine-darter in his defeat to Tommy Lishman.

The field for this month's Players Championship Finals will be confirmed following the conclusion of PC34, with the top 64 players on the yearly Players Championship rankings assured of qualification.

It's also set to be a pivotal day in the battle for World Darts Championship qualification.

articles.title: Craig Carton says Alabama is 'screwing everybody else' after Crimson Tide land at No. 5 in rankings
articles.summary: Craig Carton blasts the college football playoff rankings for placing Alabama at No. 5 while Tennessee sits at No. 13 despite a head-to-head win.
articles.body: The first College Football Playoff rankings dropped Tuesday night, and right on cue, the committee gave college football fans plenty to be mad about. Alabama somehow checked in at No. 5 while Tennessee got parked down at No. 13. Keep in mind this is just two weeks after the Vols handled the Tide head-to-head. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Craig Carton wasn't having any of the committee's nonsense Wednesday's The Craig Carton Show. "Question, question, question. Question on the floor. How is Alabama ranked fifth when Tennessee is ranked 13th? Inquiring minds want to know," Carton said. "They played each other two weeks ago. Tennessee beat them by 16 points." COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF RANKINGS: MIAMI TAKES TOP SPOT, INDIANA CRACKS TOP FIVE IN FIRST OFFICIAL RELEASE It is a fair question that has very little to do with hyping up Knoxville. Carton pointed out that Tennessee has its own flaws and probably does not belong anywhere near the top five right now. But when both programs sit at two losses, common sense suggests the team that won on the field should have the advantage. TENNESSEE DOMINATES AS ALABAMA SUFFERS FIRST BACK-TO-BACK REGULAR-SEASON LOSSES IN NEARLY TWO DECADES "Now, I'm not saying Tennessee should be a top-five program right now. They shouldn't be," he noted. "But how does Alabama, with two losses, get ranked eight spots ahead of Tennessee when they just lost to Tennessee head-to-head? " That gets to the heart of what actually frustrates people about this process. Head-to-head is not just another metric on a piece of paper, it is the only piece of evidence that was decided by the players on the field. YES, ALABAMA'S COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF RANKING IS ABSURD, BUT ONE TEAM GOT ROYALLY SCREWED BY THE COMMITTEE "Isn't head-to-head, shouldn't head-to-head, unless you're a porn star, of course, shouldn't head-to-head be the number one deciding factor when figuring out which team should be over another team? " he asked. "Then you can, of course, get into strength of schedule, the opponents, and all the other nonsense. They played against each other. I watched the game. Tennessee dominated Alabama." Yet whenever Alabama drops a couple of games, the committee seems to look for every possible reason to keep the Crimson Tide near the top. "And yet, here we are, like we always are, currying favor with the Crimson Tide," Carton pointed out. "You know, the only good thing about Alabama, not the, uh, is that a state in Alabama? It is. I'm pretty sure it's a state," he said. "The only good thing about Alabama, not the state, because I think it's a wonderful state, but the college, are those hot sorority videos that come out every September and October. You know the ones, 150 girls standing on the front porch of an old plantation house ... I love it. I love it, man. But Tennessee's got the same thing there, too." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Viral videos aside, the bottom line comes down to football, and Carton finished by giving Alabama fans a dose of reality. CFP RANKINGS: NOTRE DAME FACES SUDDEN DEATH, SEC FEELING GOOD, AND BIG TEN CLOSE TO HITTING THE PANIC BUTTON "And I've got to tell you this, I'm not saying that Tennessee got screwed, but I'm saying that Alabama's screwing everybody else," he concluded. "And Alabama is not winning a national title this year, and they should not. Sorry, Crimson Tide fans. Roll Tide. You should not be No. 5 in these first official rankings when it comes to football." articles.standfirst: Tapia y Libaak sufrieron ante Francia, mientras que ‘La Roja’ arrasó ante Emiratos Árabes.
articles.summary: Tapia y Libaak sufrieron ante Francia, mientras que ‘La Roja’ arrasó ante Emiratos Árabes.
articles.body: España no empezó con las mejores sensaciones el Mundial de pádel celebrado en Doha. Argentina, en cambio, saldó con dos triunfos convincentes sus primeras jornadas. Sin embargo, en la última fecha de la fase de grupos se han invertido los papeles. La albiceleste ha tenido un susto importante con dos de sus mejores jugadores, mientras que España ha arrasado ante Emiratos Árabes. Aunque, eso sí, ambas selecciones han pasado primeras de grupo y ya están en cuartos de final. Argentina se veía las caras con Francia y arrancaba el duelo con Agustín Tapia y Tino Libaak, que se medían a Joris y Fonteny, ambos fuera del top-100 del ranking FIP. Parecía un choque plácido para el ‘Mozart’ y la ‘Joya’, pero se les complicó desde el principio. Los franceses no daban su brazo a torcer y, contra todo pronóstico, se llevaron la primera manga por 7-5. Lejos de dejarlo en anécdota, siguieron apretando a los sudamericanos, que no lo tuvieron sencillo para remontar. En el segundo, un 6-3 y lo tuvieron que cerrar con un ajustado 6-4 en el tercero. Victoria, sí, pero dejando dudas ante un rival de mucho menor nivel como es Francia. Aunque sus siguientes partidos fueron mucho más sencillos: Franco Stupaczuk y Fede Chingotto pasaron por encima de Boronad y Robert por 6-2 y 6-1, lo mismo que Martín Di Nenno y Gonza Alfonso, que también se llevaron el triunfo ante Guichard y Blanque. España, por su parte, continúa con esa mejoría con respecto al debut ante Suecia. En el último partido de la primera fase, frente a una Emiratos Árabes mermada por la ausencia de los nacionalizados, los de Juanjo Gutiérrez fueron una apisonadora. No cedieron más de dos juegos en ninguno de los tres partidos disputados. Los primeros fueron Juan Lebrón y Javi Leal, que precisamente venía de decir en MARCA las ganas que tenía de jugar con el ‘Lobo’. Justo después, Jon Sanz y Paquito Navarro también ganaron con autoridad, recordando esa pareja que ya funcionó tan bien a finales del curso pasado. Cerraron el día Coki Nieto —que se estrena en este Mundial— junto a Mike Yanguas. Así pues, se termina la fase de grupos con las dos principales favoritas con un pleno de victorias y como primeras de grupo, clasificándose a los cuartos de final. España se medirá a Brasil y Argentina a Alemania, que pasa de ronda por primera vez en su historia en este deporte. Italia se clasificó también como líder de su grupo y Paraguay, que tenía muy buena pinta, al final se queda fuera por perder ante Suecia. En el cuadro femenino, España continúa dando espectáculo dentro y fuera de la pista. El buen rollo es la tónica dominante de la concentración de las de Carolina Navarro y lo muestran en cada pequeño momento. Además, saldan todos sus partidos con victorias abultadas. En la tercera jornada jugaron contra Brasil, con Ari Sánchez volviendo a compartir pista con Marta Ortega tras haber sido inseparables en menores. Completaron la alineación Gemma Triay con Claudia Fernández y Martina Calvo otra vez con Andrea Ustero. Todo triunfos con mucha autoridad rumbo a los cuartos de final. Igual que Argentina, que tenía una prueba de fuego contra Francia, la cual solventaron con creces con tres victorias sencillas. Países Bajos se destapa como la revelación al tumbar a la Portugal de Sofía Araujo y así pasar como primeras, evitándose a Argentina. Italia, al igual que en chicos, también avanza de ronda con Suecia como segunda.
