articles.summary: The Nashville Predators are paying tribute to one of Music City's biggest stars during their upcoming game against the St. Louis Blues.
articles.body:
The Nashville Predators are paying tribute to one of Music City's biggest stars during their upcoming game against the St. Louis Blues.

The Predators' Hometown Remix jerseys will feature a commemorative patch to honor Grammy-winning artist Dolly Parton, who passed away earlier this year. The patch has a navy border around a gold butterfly. The country music star often used the butterfly as a symbol following her 1974 hit "Love is Like a Butterfly."

The jerseys, which will be worn during pregame warmups, will also have "Dolly" on the nameplate above each player's number.

Predators goaltender Juuse Saros is also honoring Parton with his new hometown remix mask:

The jerseys will be auctioned through the Nashville Predators Foundation after the game, and all proceeds will benefit Dolly Parton's Imagination Library and the Monroe Carell Jr. Children's Hospital at Vanderbilt.

Parton, a Tennessee native, won 11 Grammy Awards and three Emmy Awards while selling more than 100 records throughout her illustrious career. Her Dollywood Foundation helped deliver millions of children's books across the world.

"It is an incredible honor for us to celebrate Dolly Parton this Saturday with a specialty patch on our Hometown Remix jerseys," Nashville Predators CEO Sean Henry said. "When working on the design for our jerseys, Dolly was one of our inspirations, given her legacy and how she was a trailblazer for so many in the country music industry. We are thrilled to honor her and grateful to give back to both Monroe Carell and her Imagination Library, an organization that has and continues to support so many not only in Tennessee, but around the world."

The NHL revealed all 32 Hometown Remix jerseys on Monday. The jerseys are intended to honor something unique about each franchise, and the Predators will wear their Hometown Remix jerseys in 10 games throughout the 2026-27 season.

articles.title: Indy Showcase, new college volleyball event, to help kick off season in 2027. What we know
articles.summary: College volleyball continues to grow around the Circle City, and in 2027 it will bring a new event to the city that once hosted the Final Four.
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS — College volleyball is returning to Gainbridge Fieldhouse with a two-day early season showcase.

The Indiana Sports Corp. announced Wednesday evening that the Indy Showcase will feature a four-team event Aug. 28-29, 2027. Similar to the men's college basketball Indy Classic, the event will serve as a fundraiser supporting Sports Corp. missions, according to a release.

Indianapolis once hosted a Final Four in 1987 at Market Square Arena, and college volleyball returned downtown on Oct. 16, 2025 when Purdue beat Indiana in the Monon Spike Match , which drew 6,477 fans on a sectional volleyball night , no less. The explosion of college volleyball reaching the Circle City is perhaps not a surprise.

The inaugural Big Ten volleyball tournament will be hosted at the nearby Fishers Events Center from Nov. 20-25.

"You can't keep up with the explosion right now that is volleyball," Purdue coach Dave Shondell said last season. "And I think that you, fortunately people in the media are finally getting behind it — whether it be TV or print or on the internet — but it's hard to keep up with all the things that are going on in the attendance records that are being broken. You watch it every night you want to on TV, so it's a great time to be in volleyball."

The Indy Showcase will have information at a later date about the four teams, match times and broadcast information. However, it will bring four matches downtown early in the season, a rising trend across the sport.

The AVCA First Serve Showcase has become popular with Big Ten members Wisconsin (in Milwaukee) and Nebraska being featured prominently. Other events have blossomed out of those successes, both in television viewership and attendance.

Consider Indiana played at the Broadway Block Party in Nashville this season, and Purdue played in the State Farm Volleyball Showcase at the Sanford Pentagon in South Dakota and the Paradise Invitational in the Bahamas. Both teams were part of the Big Ten/SEC challenge, too.

Now, Indianapolis is getting involved with the Sports Corp. and its mission to make Indianapolis the women's sports capital of the world by 2050. Perhaps that means a Final Four in the near future.

articles.title: Real Madrid’s Hot Start Under Mourinho Is Nothing New
articles.summary: A third of Madrid’s best starts in La Liga over last 35 years have been with the Portuguese maestro at the helm
articles.body:
Real Madrid's 0-3 victory over Racing Santander on Sunday was the team's fourth consecutive win in La Liga, taking José Mourinho's side to 27 points through the first 11 matches. That marks the 17th time in 96 seasons in Spain's first division that Madrid has managed 27 or more points at this early stage.

Mourinho has been manager on three of those 17 occasions. His Madrid team recorded 29 points through 11 matches in 2010/11 and totaled 28 points through 11 matchdays on the way to a record-setting 100-point season in 2011/12. Despite being in charge for less than 5% of Madrid's seasons in La Liga, Mourinho has overseen nearly a fifth of the club's best starts in Spain's top flight—a testament to his ability to get the team functioning quickly. In fact, if we look at the last 35 La Liga seasons, Madrid has managed 27+ points through 11 matches nine times, a third of which have come with the Portuguese maestro at the helm.

Madrid has scored 28 times through the first 11 league matches, equaling the 28 goals recorded under Carlo Ancelotti in the same period of the 2022/23 season. You have to go back to 2016/17—when Madrid scored 31 times in its first 11 matches, the last season Cristiano Ronaldo was available to start a La Liga campaign—to find a better goal-scoring start. To further illustrate Madrid's strong form in attack, the team is creating an average of 4 big chances per match in La Liga this season, the most through the first 11 matches since it averaged 4.2 in 2017/18 (though Madrid that season had yet to face either Barcelona or Atlético Madrid at a similar point).

Curiously, in two of the three seasons in which Madrid logged its best starts through the first 11 matches—10 wins and 1 draw in each—the club ultimately failed to lift the La Liga trophy. The 1991/92 campaign saw the club open with 10 wins and 1 draw under Serbian manager Radomir Antić, with Madrid's first defeat not arriving until the 16th league match against Atlético Madrid. Antić was fired that January despite Madrid holding a 7-point lead; club president Ramón Mendoza stated publicly that he was unhappy with the team's unconvincing style of play.

In 2022/23, Ancelotti's men managed 10 victories and one draw through 11 matches in Spain's top flight, with Madrid not tasting defeat until the 13th match, a 3-2 loss to Rayo Vallecano at Vallecas. That match will be remembered for the continuous fouls on Vinícius Júnior—with and without the ball—that went unpunished for Rayo's players.

Madrid did manage to win La Liga in 1968/69 under legendary manager Miguel Muñoz after starting league play with 10 wins and 1 draw, losing only once all season. That defeat came against Elche, 0-1, in the 28th match of a 30-game league competition. It was the only match Amancio Amaro—Pichichi that season—missed in league play.

articles.title: One of college soccer's winningest coaches is leaving Rice after the season
articles.summary: A national search will begin immediately, as the coach plans to continue coaching and build another program.
articles.body:
Brian Lee, one of the most successful coaches in collegiate soccer history and current coach of the Rice Owls women's soccer team , will step down at season's end.

The Owls, who finished 4th in the conference with a 4-4-2 record, will continue their season in the American Conference Championship against defending conference champions UTSA on Sunday. According to Rice interim athletic director Eric George and Lee, the two agreed that the head coach will assist with the transition through the end of the year, including supporting current student-athletes and recruits.

"I am proud of what our players and staff accomplished together at Rice, on the field, in the classroom and in the Houston community," said Lee in a statement to Chron. "After thoughtful conversations with Eric, we agreed this is the right time for both the program and for me to take the next step. I am grateful to Rice for the opportunity, and I am excited to continue coaching and to build the next great program."

In a statement, the university said it will begin a national search for the program's next head coach immediately.

Rice finished its 2026 regular season with a 6-7-5 record, as Lee compiled a 76-52-23 record in seven seasons as the Owls' head coach after being hired in 2019 . Lee was twice named his conference's coach of the year (2020, 2024), and six of his players earned conference player of the year honors. In 2021 , Mijke Roelfsema became the first player in school history to earn first-team All-American honors.

"We are grateful for Brian's dedication to Rice and our soccer program throughout his tenure," said George in a statement to Chron. "He has recruited and mentored incredible student-athletes who have represented Rice with integrity and excellence in the classroom, community, and on the field. His teams have helped set a new standard of excellence for Rice soccer, and we wish Brian every success in the next chapter of his career."

The Cheltenham, England native's career record of 363-232-78 (.610 win percentage) across 33 seasons at Furman, LSU and Rice places him among the winningest coaches in Division I women's soccer history. Lee, 55, will likely have plenty of suitors for his coaching services either collegiately or at the professional level.

articles.title: Saints’ Jordyn Tyson, Kelvin Banks Jr. return to practice but there’s a catch
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints received some encouraging injury news Wednesday, as rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and offensive tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. returned t...
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints received some encouraging injury news Wednesday, as rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and offensive tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. returned to practice on a limited basis. However, neither player is officially back just yet, as the team still has a decision to make regarding their availability.

Head coach Kellen Moore also confirmed that New Orleans opened their 21-day practice windows, giving the Saints three weeks to activate each player from injured reserve.

Opening the practice windows is an important step in their respective recoveries, but it does not guarantee either player will immediately return to action this weekend. The Saints will have to evaluate how both players progress before making a final decision. If they are not activated within the 21-day window, they will remain on injured reserve for the rest of the season.

Tyson's potential return is encouraging for a New Orleans offense that could use another playmaker at wide receiver. The rookie has an opportunity to make an immediate impact once he is cleared to play, especially alongside Chris Olave.

Olave has been one of the Saints' primary receiving options, and adding Tyson to the equation could give the offense another dimension. The rookie has spent time watching and studying while sidelined, which could help him get up to speed as he works toward returning to game action. Having two capable receivers on the field together would give New Orleans more flexibility in the passing game and prevent opposing defenses from focusing as heavily on Olave.

Banks' return to practice is equally important for the offensive line. The Saints need to get healthier up front, and having their young tackle work his way back provides another potential boost to the protection in front of the quarterback.

For now, New Orleans will have to be patient. Both players have taken an encouraging step toward returning, but the next three weeks will determine whether they are ready to contribute again.

articles.title: Lando Norris blasts F1 top speed limiters: “We should easily go quicker than a motorbike”
articles.summary: Lando Norris blasts F1's limiter for ruining racing at the Mexico City GP, comparing the cars to MotoGP bikes
articles.body:
Riding in the slipstream is supposed to be the ultimate offensive weapon for a Formula 1 driver. But according to Lando Norris , the current technical regulations have turned the draft into something a little less useful.

Trapped in a train throughout the Mexico City Grand Prix, the McLaren driver vented his frustrations over F1's car. He argued that the artificial ceiling, created by a cap on battery on battery deployment, makes late-braking divebombs and straight-line passes practically impossible against evenly matched cars.

"I mean the main thing with overtaking is you just have the limiter on," Norris explained in the paddock. "Like you literally have a limiter that stops you from going over a speed, so it doesn't matter if you come out two tenths behind the guy, you just hit the limiter and the same limiter as them, and then you cannot do anything, so it kind of ruins racing."

The 2026 regulations heavily feature active aerodynamics, using a low-drag Straight Mode to maximise velocity on massive stretches of track such as the 1.2-kilometre front straight at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez. But Norris firmly believes the governing body is keeping the cars on an unnecessary leash, pointing directly to the two-wheeled motorsport world as proof.

"It's something that they need to improve for next season," the Brit demanded. "Especially when motorbikes go 370, and you don't have a seat belt or anything, and we should easily be able to go quicker than a motorbike, you know."

He added that the artificial cap fundamentally damaged the on-track product on Sunday.

Pressing the issue, a journalist asked if future engine rule tweaks might naturally solve the top speed plateau. The Woking star quickly shut down the theory, insisting that powertrain modifications are completely irrelevant as long as the hard limit exists.

"No, I mean that's got nothing to do with it," he clarified. "We still achieve the same top speeds when you have Straight Mode, and in Straight Mode and with the same power next year you still achieve the same top speed, so you just need to make the limiter higher. It's as simple as that."

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lando Norris, McLaren

Despite his intense criticism of the rulebook, the 26-year-old refused to use the speed cap as a total excuse for missing the podium. Recognising that a massive raw pace delta was required to execute a pass in Mexico, he pointed the finger squarely at McLaren's own garage.

"Nothing ruined today," he confessed. "It's just you have to be very quick to pass. No one could get any overtakes unless you're a lot quicker. So nothing to blame but our poor Saturday."

articles.title: New NHL Report Identifies Teams Hesitating on Dylan Larkin Trade
articles.summary: NHL insider Chris Johnston identifies four teams showing limited urgency in Dylan Larkin trade discussions, creating another challenge for the Red Wings.
articles.body:
The Detroit Red Wings have spent months trying to find a trade that works for Dylan Larkin, but the latest NHL reporting suggests their biggest problem might be more complicated than his unwillingness to approve additional destinations.

Some of the teams Larkin is already willing to join apparently aren't in much of a hurry to acquire him.

According to NHL insider Chris Johnston, four organizations on Larkin's approved 10-team trade list are taking a cautious approach to negotiations, creating another obstacle for interim general manager Shawn Horcoff.

And considering Detroit's determination to secure a substantial return for its former captain, that's a significant problem.

Four Teams Reportedly Taking Cautious Approach to Dylan Larkin Trade

During Monday's episode of The Chris Johnston Show , Johnston identified four teams that aren't showing much urgency to complete a Larkin trade.

Johnston characterized those clubs as "not desperate to get something done," suggesting they are waiting to better understand what acquiring Larkin would require.

The report does not establish that any of the four teams has definitively ruled out acquiring Larkin. It also doesn't mean they have all made offers that Detroit rejected.

Instead, it indicates those organizations are approaching the situation carefully rather than aggressively pursuing an immediate agreement.

For Horcoff, that creates a difficult negotiating environment.

The Red Wings can contact 10 acceptable destinations, but having permission to trade Larkin to a team doesn't guarantee that organization is willing to pay Detroit's asking price.

Larkin's trade protection has been one of the biggest obstacles throughout this process.

The 30-year-old center carries an $8.7 million annual salary-cap hit and remains under contract through the 2030-31 season.

Those circumstances make him an attractive long-term addition for the right organization, but they also limit how easily a contender can fit him into its roster and payroll.

And Detroit isn't interested in giving him away.

As we previously reported when examining Washington's salary-cap challenge , acquiring Larkin would likely require the Capitals to send salary back while also assembling a return attractive enough for Horcoff.

That combination makes an already complicated trade even more difficult.

The same basic issue applies throughout the market.

A team might appreciate Larkin's ability to play significant minutes, contribute offensively, and handle important defensive assignments without believing he's worth sacrificing multiple young assets.

Another organization might have the prospects Detroit wants but lack sufficient flexibility to take on his contract.

And some contenders simply may not consider another center a pressing need.

That's what makes Johnston's latest reporting so concerning for the Red Wings.

Detroit doesn't need 10 teams that would theoretically accept Larkin.

It needs multiple organizations genuinely motivated to compete for him.

Dylan Larkin's Refusal to Expand Trade List Creates Bigger Problem

The timing of this report is especially noteworthy because of another development involving Larkin's representatives.

As we reported Tuesday night , NHL insider Pierre LeBrun revealed that Horcoff recently approached Larkin's camp about expanding his list of approved destinations.

According to LeBrun, Larkin's representatives maintained that 10 acceptable destinations should provide Detroit with enough possibilities to complete a trade.

But Johnston's assessment suggests that the actual number of motivated buyers could be considerably smaller.

If Washington, Tampa Bay, New Jersey, and Utah aren't particularly aggressive, Detroit has fewer realistic options than the original list suggests.

That doesn't mean none of those teams could eventually complete a deal.

It does mean Horcoff cannot necessarily count on them to create the type of bidding competition that might force an interested organization to improve its offer.

Meanwhile, reportedly interested teams outside Larkin's approved destinations remain unable to acquire him without his consent.

For a franchise trying to obtain a young center or other significant building blocks in return, that imbalance matters.

Shawn Horcoff Has Little Reason to Panic

Despite the frustrating circumstances, there is another side to this situation.

Detroit isn't obligated to accept an inferior return simply because Larkin wants to leave.

Following the decision to suspend the former captain without pay, Horcoff explained that the Red Wings were prepared to wait for a satisfactory deal .

Larkin remains a valuable player on a long-term contract, and acquiring a comparable center would be extremely difficult.

If Detroit moves him for an underwhelming package, the organization could spend years trying to replace the production and responsibilities he leaves behind.

That would be particularly damaging for a franchise still attempting to establish itself as a consistent playoff contender.

Horcoff must also consider what type of return would actually improve the Red Wings.

A package built around draft picks might look impressive on paper, but it wouldn't necessarily address the team's immediate need for established NHL talent.

On the other hand, refusing every offer that doesn't contain a potential franchise cornerstone could keep the situation unresolved indefinitely.

The Red Wings Need Buyers, Not Just Approved Destinations

Johnston's latest report reveals an important weakness in Detroit's negotiating position.

The problem isn't necessarily that nobody wants Larkin.

It's that some of the organizations he would accept may not want him badly enough to offer what Detroit considers fair compensation.

Minnesota has reportedly remained aggressive, but its willingness to pursue Larkin doesn't automatically give Horcoff the leverage created by multiple determined buyers.

And unless another approved destination becomes more serious, Detroit could continue facing the same difficult choice.

Accept a return that falls short of its expectations, or hold onto a player who has made it clear he wants to continue his career elsewhere.

For now, there is no confirmed agreement with any team, and no verified change to Larkin's list of approved destinations.

The biggest question is no longer how many teams Larkin would join. It's how many are actually willing to pay Detroit's price.

Until that changes, Horcoff's patience may be tested even further.

articles.title: Chargers’ Jim Harbaugh defends Justin Herbert after Quentin Lake’s ‘deli meat’ diss
articles.summary: Turns out there’s another LA battle going on outside of the mayor race. But this one involves a clapback from Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh. A...
articles.body:
Turns out there's another LA battle going on outside of the mayor race. But this one involves a clapback from Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh . All stemming from a "deli meat" diss Los Angeles Rams safety Quentin Lake handed to Justin Herbert.

The Rams captain appeared on the St. Brown Brothers podcast to take a dig at the struggling Bolts quarterback.

"He was throwing deli meat out there. He's seeing ghosts, I'm not gonna lie. We knew we were gonna get a couple," Lake said in describing the two-interception outing they created on Sunday, leading to the 24-9 Rams rout.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Harbaugh, however, strongly disagreed with the Lake assessment.

"As far as anyone's opinion, I don't see that. Everybody's entitled to their opinion, that's not what I see," Harbaugh told reporters on Wednesday.

He later got asked what he has seen out of Herbert amid his struggles.

"Pass game, I thought he did his job exceptionally well. Two throws he'd like to have back," Harbaugh said.

Still, the Bolts never found consistent offensive rhythm in the LA battle. Herbert got kept out of the end zone along with the other Chargers skill position players. The losing Los Angeles team settled for field goal to put points on the board, making it nine straight quarters that the Bolts haven't crossed the end zone.

Worse is the Chargers and Rams are now going in opposite directions. The latter finds themselves at 4-4 now following a rough 2-4 start. But the Bolts remain the NFL's lone winless team at 0-7 overall.

articles.title: Maxx Crosby makes his Raiders feelings clear amid constant trade rumors
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders star defensive end Maxx Crosby has made his feelings clear about his future with the organization amid constant trade rumors as the team pr...
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders star defensive end Maxx Crosby has made his feelings clear about his future with the organization amid constant trade rumors as the team prepares for its Week 9 road matchup against the San Francisco 49ers (6-1) .

Despite ongoing speculation surrounding his future in Las Vegas, Crosby reiterated his commitment to the franchise Wednesday, making it clear that he has no desire to leave.

Raiders reporter Levi Edwards shared Crosby's comments on X, formerly known as Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I love being a Raider, I've said that about a million times, this is where I want to be."

Crosby's comments come as the Raiders (4-4) look to build momentum following their 38-33 Week 8 victory over the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on Sunday. The win snapped a four-game losing streak that included defeats against the Kansas City Chiefs, Buffalo Bills, New England Patriots and Los Angeles Rams.

The veteran pass rusher has remained a significant part of Las Vegas' defense throughout the 2026 campaign. Through eight games, Crosby has recorded 22 total tackles, including nine solo and 13 assisted stops, along with three sacks, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery and one pass defended.

Crosby also registered four tackles and one sack in the Raiders' victory over the Jets, helping the team return to .500 ahead of its upcoming divisional matchup against San Francisco.

Maxx Crosby remains committed to Raiders after bizarre offseason

Crosby's latest comments come after an unusual offseason that nearly resulted in his departure from Las Vegas.

The Raiders previously agreed to trade Crosby to the Baltimore Ravens in exchange for two first-round draft picks, including Baltimore's No. 14 overall selection in the 2026 NFL Draft and a 2027 first-rounder.

However, the Ravens unexpectedly backed out of the agreement following concerns surrounding Crosby's surgically repaired knee during his physical examination.

The failed trade generated considerable speculation about Crosby's future, particularly after the defensive end revealed that his visit to Baltimore featured several unusual interactions with the organization's leadership.

During an episode of The Rush With Maxx Crosby, he described an awkward meeting with Ravens head coach Jesse Minter and explained that he did not meet with the team's general manager during his visit.

Despite the uncertainty surrounding the collapsed agreement, Crosby ultimately remained with the Raiders entering the 2026 season.

His continued commitment comes as Las Vegas attempts to establish consistency under head coach Klint Kubiak following a disappointing 3-14 campaign in 2025.

With the Raiders back at .500 and preparing for another difficult matchup against the 49ers, Crosby's comments reinforce his desire to remain with the franchise rather than pursue an opportunity elsewhere.

For now, the Raiders will look to build on their recent victory when they visit San Francisco on Sunday.

articles.title: Eagles reportedly making quarterback change amidst struggles
articles.summary: The Eagles’ season has been falling apart for weeks. Now they’re making a change at the most important position on the field, just two days after saying they...
articles.body:
The Eagles' season has been falling apart for weeks. Now they're making a change at the most important position on the field, just two days after saying they wouldn't.

Philadelphia is turning to its third starting quarterback of the season. And it's a player who was on another team's practice squad less than a month ago.

Amidst a six-game losing streak, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Joe Milton will start for the Eagles against the Giants on Sunday. He'll replace Tanner McKee, who started the last three games.

That's a sharp reversal from what Nick Sirianni said on Monday. When asked if a change at quarterback was on the table, the Eagles coach was clear.

"Again, you know, Tanner's our guy. We're not making any changes there," Sirianni said, in his Monday press conference . "And you know, again, how do we find solutions? That could be within scheme, you know, that could be within how we, you know, our schedule is, practice plays, right? And so everything's on the table for us in that aspect."

Apparently, everything included the quarterback.

McKee completed 63.2% of his passes for 638 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions in his three starts, according to ESPN. The Eagles lost all three.

The Eagles signed Milton off the Cowboys' practice squad on Oct. 16. He spent last season as Dak Prescott's backup in Dallas after being traded there by the Patriots, who drafted him in the sixth round in 2024.

On Wednesday, before the news broke, Sirianni praised Milton's work ethic. "He works extremely hard. You know, he is, he's always in the building, doing the extra things, and yeah, I like his progression," Sirianni said .

The quarterback carousel started when Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve in October after doctors found multiple blood clots in both of his lungs. Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the season.

The situation drew widespread backlash after it was revealed Hurts still played after being hospitalized . The NFL was reportedly "furious" with the Eagles over how it was handled.

Things haven't gotten any better on the field. After a 2-0 start, the Eagles have dropped six straight and sit last in the NFC East at 2-6.

After Sunday night's 27-10 loss to the Commanders, Sirianni put the blame on himself , saying, "I'm not doing a good enough job right now."

articles.title: Offseason open chat and discussion: November 4
articles.summary: Even though the season is over, there is a lot going on over the next few weeks to discuss.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Braves have concluded their season, but there is still quite a bit going on that could directly have an impact on them. We have awards rolling in, salary cap discussions, potential free agent signings and trades, etc.

Keep an eye out for the Rookie of the Year announcement on November 9th. Didier Fuentes likely will not win, but it will be interesting to see how many down votes he gets. It is arbitrary in nature, but it can be fun to discuss what the outcome will be.

Manager of the Year will be announced on November 10th. The term finalist is a bit deceiving because the voting has already decided, but all three NL "finalists" have a legitimate reason to have received the top three total votes. Mattingly took a team look destined to fail and turned the season around. Weiss took a team that missed the playoffs last season and brought them to a NLE division win, and Murphy once again led a dominant Brewers team that led MLB in wins (postseason was not factored into voting).

We also have Chris Sale in the mix for Cy Young. He likely did not win, but like Fuentes it will be fun to see how voters placed him.

There has been a new update on salary cap and salary floor as well. It is always fun to hear people's thoughts on this subject.

The MLB General Manager Meetings start next week on November 9th in Las Vegas. We don't typically see a ton happen at these meetings, but they do typically set the groundwork for trades and evaluation of free agent markets. There is a small chance we see some minor additions at this time.

Let's talk about these subjects or whatever else is on your mind in the comments.

articles.title: 3 things for the Rams to know about the Commanders
articles.summary: Here's what the Rams can learn about the Commanders from their first seven games of the season.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to play the Washington Commanders this week , and if the Rams wish to achieve a winning record for the first time this season, they will need to deal with a team that refuses to capitulate. Here are three lessons the Rams can learn about the Commanders from their first seven games this season.

Washington may not win, but it won't be for a lack of trying

Washington's effort level this season has been unreal, and for a team that has been struggling, there's a reason why head coach Dan Quinn's seat isn't as hot as others in the NFL. The Commanders play with a passion and an attitude that goes above and beyond. It feels like there's a real belief within the organization behind what they're about, and if they can clean up their on-field operation – especially with penalties – they could turn the corner.

They do get sloppy at times, and their list of injured players doesn't help. Wins may be hard to find in the nation's capital, but that doesn't mean the organization is packing it in. They play with a fire, especially at home, where this game will be taking place.

Stefon Diggs has been a godsend for the Washington Commanders offense, especially now that Terry McLaurin is out for the season. Despite being one of the last big-name free agents left on the board this offseason, primarily due to legal issues that Diggs squashed this summer, his production is the only thing keeping Washington in the hunt for the postseason.

He has 27 receptions for 252 yards and five touchdowns through six games played, and he was on the field for their only two wins of the season. Due to his elbow injury and how that has impacted his play, quarterback Jayden Daniels is no longer the biggest threat within Washington's offense. Diggs is.

There isn't anything special about Washington's operation, and that's why they're 2-4-1 this season. They should be 3-4, if we're being honest, but we need to dive deeper beyond the record. They had some struggles early, but they beat the Seattle Seahawks and played the San Francisco 49ers close.

They are really well coached and are outperforming the expectations that their roster provides. They do the little things well enough to drag games into deep water, and they're finding their footing. The Rams can ill-afford to come up short on the details. Primarily, executing early offensively, maintaining solid pass-rushing lanes that prohibit Daniels from stepping up into space, and avoiding turnovers/special teams letdowns.

If the Rams try to be too exotic in their overall approach, Washington has the ability to make teams pay for their oversights.

articles.title: Parkinson's pride as Wrexham deliver against Boro
articles.summary: Phil Parkinson spoke about the pride he took from Wrexham's display as they secured a 2-0 win over Championship leaders Middlesbrough at the Racecourse Groun...
articles.body:
Phil Parkinson feels his Wrexham side delivered a performance the club's fans, staff and owners could relate to as they defeated Championship leaders Middlesbrough 2-0 at the Racecourse Ground.

Second half goals from George Thomason and Ollie Rathbone earned the Red Dragons a crucial victory as Boro's 11-game unbeaten league run was ended.

It was the perfect response from Wrexham on the back of what was a lacklustre display against Sheffield United at Bramall Lane five days earlier.

"As I said to you after the game on Friday, all I ever want and all the owners want is the honesty in the performance which our fans can relate to," said Parkinson.

"That's why there's been a great connection between the supporters and the players, owners and myself because, in general, they've seen honesty and commitment and that's what the club's all about.

"I'm just really pleased. We're not getting carried away, but we upset a good team tonight."

The Wrexham boss added: "Middlesbrough know they've been in a game tonight.

"My, Steve [assistant coach, Parkin] and the rest of the staff's mantra since day one is that if anyone comes to the Racecourse, they've got to know that they've been in one hell of a game, and I think the Middlesbrough players know that tonight."

Speaking in his post-match press conference after the victory over table toppers Boro, Parkinson - a boyhood Middlesbrough supporter - revealed his father has recently been unwell.

The 58-year-old boss paid a touching tribute to his father in the aftermath of the victory.

"I'd just like to make a special mention to my dad, he's been ill over the last few weeks," he explained.

"I know how much that performance will have lifted him tonight, watching back home in Stockton-on-Tees with a lot of his friends, Middlesbrough fans as well.

"I just can't wait to speak to him on the way back."

Sam Smith was absent from the matchday squad for the victory over Kim Hellberg's side.

The striker sustained a knee injury in the latter stages of Wrexham's 1-0 loss to Sheffield United at Bramall Lane on Friday night.

Prior to the win against Middlesbrough, Parkinson confirmed the 28-year-old was set for a spell on the sidelines.

In the aftermath of the contest, the manager revealed Smith is set to undergo surgery next week and will be sidelined for the remainder of the campaign.

"Unfortunately with Sam, he's done his cruciate," Parkinson added.

"He's going to be out for nine months and faces the operation next Wednesday."

Wrexham have been dealt numerous injury issues this season, with Josh Windass, Nathan Broadhead, Liberato Cacace and Callum O'Hare among those currently sidelined.

But Parkinson said he would not accept players feeling sorry for themselves, something he felt may have been the case at Sheffield United last time out.

"We've had injuries in other years, we've had setbacks, we've always dug deep," Parkinson said.

"I felt at Sheffield United we looked like a team that had almost taken one blow too many, but I'm not accepting that."

articles.title: Jacoby Brissett trade gives Zay Flowers and the Ravens' offense a fantasy lifeline
articles.summary: Jacoby Brissett looks ready to save the day for fantasy football managers after reportedly being dealt to the Ravens.
articles.body:
What originally began as a beautiful dream for the Ravens (and fantasy football managers invested in the team) devolved into a nightmare over the course of a few weeks. Zay Flowers, Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry started the season on a note where many were extremely excited for what was to come.

Unfortunately, that bright future never came to pass, as Flowers dealt with a hamstring injury, only to return to see both his quarterbacks — first Lamar Jackson, now Snoop Huntley (and Lamar again) — suffer injuries. Huntley is done for the season with a turf toe injury, while Jackson has been placed on IR with a thumb ailment that required surgery and could also end his season.

Thoughts of Flowers being a top-five receiver, of Henry once again laughing in the face of Father Time, went right out the window.

Or maybe not? Yahoo Sports analysts Nate Tice and Matt Harmon discuss the major move the Ravens made to try to save their season in the video above.

After losing Jackson and Huntley to injuries on Sunday, the 4-4 Ravens didn't throw in the towel, reportedly opting to trade for the veter an Brissett . Now, Brissett just finished getting benched by the Cardinals, but we have seen in the past that he not only can keep some fantasy stars afloat, but he can help them reach their weekly ceilings. We can't just forget that it was with Jacoby Brissett throwing the ball that we witnessed the rise of Trey McBride and Michael Wilson as weekly fantasy starters.

The Cardinals haven't been that potent, garbage-time-crushing offense this season, as the team has had many (of the usual) issues. I think we can all agree that the Ravens are a better-run system than the Cardinals. Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's system has already proven itself to be a boon to Flowers and Henry, no matter who's been at quarterback between Jackson and Huntley.

Brissett won't be able to help the Ravens or fantasy managers this week since the deal won't be finalized before Baltimore hosts the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday — rookie Joe Fagnano will get the nod at QB. However, here's hoping Brissett decides to let it fly again as part of this fantasy-friendly offense.

articles.title: Craig Luschenat on what player enhancement means to Boston Celtics
articles.summary: "I would just say it's our job to basically put a plan in place for each guy," said the Celtics assistant.
articles.body:
Craig Luschenat has made a name for himself with the Boston Celtics as one of the NBA's best player development coaches (or as they call such a position in the Celtics organization, a player enhancement coach). But much as Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla tends to do, Luschenat refuses to take sole credit for the successes we have seen with Boston in such an ambit, instead crediting the full bench of Boston assistants for any evident enhancements.

As to the meaning behind using "player enhancement" instead of "player development," the Celtics assistant related that he does not "have a definition, that's for sure" in a recent interview with the team-produced "View From the Rafters" podcast.

"I would just say it's our job to basically put a plan in place for each guy and then just try and execute that plan," added Luschenat.

"I think we put big emphasis on how we can develop our guys," said the Celtics assistant. "We look at our guys from every different lens, from mental performance, strength, and conditioning (to) what the analytics say, what the film says, what the nutrition says."

"And then we essentially try to put a plan in place and try and execute it. So … it's been a good few years here, but we don't have all the answers, and we're still trying to get better."

articles.title: Former NFC star JP Pickles seizes opportunity as Mercer’s starting QB
articles.summary: After waiting for his turn, Mercer quarterback JP Pickles is leading the Bears on a winning streak this season.
articles.body:
JP Pickles knows the value of being ready when opportunity arrives.

The former North Florida Christian star transferred from UTEP to Mercer in 2025 to be closer to home, spent his first season in a limited role and opened this year as the Bears ' backup behind a former Florida State quarterback. When his opportunity finally arrived, Pickles seized it and hasn't looked back.

The junior was named the SoCon Offensive Player of the Week for the second time this season after scoring four touchdowns in Mercer's 28-19 comeback win over The Citadel last Saturday, Oct. 31.

Pickles threw for 234 yards and three touchdowns on 17-for-20 passing with no interceptions and added 46 rushing yards and an additional touchdown. Trailing 10-0 at the half, Pickles completed 10 of 12 passes for 189 yards and led the Bears to four scoring drives in their five second-half possessions.

Winners of five straight, Mercer (7-2, 4-1 SoCon) opens a pivotal two-game conference road trip on Saturday at No. 25 Chattanooga (6-3, 5-1) at Finley Stadium.

For Pickles, the decision to transfer closer to home has proved to be exactly what he was looking for. His father also played basketball at Mercer, located three hours from Tallahassee in Macon, Georgia, for two seasons.

"I wanted to get closer to home and so I got into the transfer portal and Mercer," Pickles said. "I believe, was the first or second school I heard from. I've known about Mercer my whole life and then I took a visit here and I really liked it. So I ended up coming here."

Pickles, Mercer looks for strong finish as regular season closes

Pickles' breakthrough reinforces one of football's oldest lessons: You can't control when the opportunity arrives.

He was the backup quarterback last season to Braden Atkinson, who won the Jerry Rice Award as the top freshman in the FCS, throwing for 3,611 yards and 34 touchdowns. Atkinson transferred to Oregon State, where he's enjoying another breakout season. Pickles then entered this year as the backup to FSU transfer Jaylen King, who started well but cooled off.

Pickles' mindset never changed as he waited his turn.

"I was a backup but I was preparing to start if anything happened," Pickles said.

Across his games leading the offense against Abilene Christian, Western Carolina, Samford, and The Citadel, the athletic Pickles has guided the Bears to a 4-0 record while displaying his dual-threat efficiency. He has combined for 10 touchdowns (5 passing, 5 rushing) while averaging 262.3 yards of total offense per game.

Mercer e n ters a demanding final stretch with three regular-season games remaining, beginning at Chattanooga (6-3, 5-1). The Bears then travel to Tennessee Tech before returning home to close the regular season against ETSU.

While Pickles knows the challenge only gets tougher from here, he points to his team's strengths. He credits Mercer's success to a complementary formula: a defense that consistently puts the offense in favorable situations and a running game that has given the Bears confidence against any opponent.

"As a team, you know, we're really good on defense," Pickles said.

"They do a lot of things, and it's nice to have them helping us out, you know, getting us in good field position. We've got a really good run game. We kind of found that out at Georgia Tech. ... Ever since then, we've kind of known that we can run the ball on anyone. And we also have some really good threats on the outside. Brayden Smith, who's a four-year starter here at Mercer. He's one of the best receivers in FCS right now."

Jim Henry is Tallahassee Democrat sports editor. Email him at jjhenry@tallahassee.com .

articles.title: Look: Myles Garrett officially returns to practice for Rams
articles.summary: Myles Garrett has been designated to return from IR and is back at practice with the Rams ahead of their Week 9 game.
articles.body:
Myles Garrett missed the Los Angeles Rams ' last seven games while on injured reserve, but he's inching toward a long-awaited return to the field. The Rams have designated Garrett to return from IR, which means he's back at practice and his 21-day window has officially opened.

The Rams now have three weeks to decide whether to activate Garrett off IR, which they obviously plan to do. He can continue practicing throughout the 21-day window until he's activated.

The Rams shared a video of Garrett heading back onto the practice field for the first time since Week 1, marking his official return.

Garrett underwent knee surgery after the Rams' season opener, which landed him on injured reserve. He's been out of action ever since, leaving a void on defense. Byron Young and Josaiah Stewart have been solid at outside linebacker but there's no replacing a two-time Defensive Player of the Year.

It's unclear if Garrett will play against the Commanders this Sunday but returning to practice is unquestionably a step in the right direction.

articles.title: Oxford United 2-0 Reading: Player Ratings
articles.summary: The Royals failed to rise to the challenge of a local derby on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
Steady in the first half, collecting a few shots that came down the middle. Got down well to his right to stop a long low drive from Oxford United in the 63rd minute.

Deserved much better from his defence for both goals, and with one going in off the post and one going in at close range, it's tough to find much blame for Pereira.

Had a nasty moment for the second goal but was otherwise decent. Failed to track his runner across the box for that second goal, allowing Missanga an easy finish.

Had some great moments in transition in the first half, getting high up the field and into the box. Skipped past the Oxford full-back before feeding Josh Stokes for a shot in a fine moment at the end of the first half.

Busy out of possession as he always is, stepping to balls and allowing Dorsett to play the covering position.

Stepped too hard in the second half and was booked for a fifth time this season for a late slide. Will be suspended for the next league game as a result.

Made the initial mistake for Oxford's best chance of the half, getting sucked toward the ball and letting the pass go between him and Roberts. Recovered well to help shield the ball to Pereira.

Won a foul for Reading in a good spot high up on the left side toward the end of the first half.

Stabbed a backheel at the ball during a goalmouth scramble, and was unlucky not to see his creative effort find the back of the net.

Protected the ball better than many around him for Reading, completing 80% of his passes on a night when many players struggled to hit 50%.

Did a fantastic job of drawing fouls in the early stages when Oxford pressed high up the field aggressively. Made a goal-saving intervention when Oxford almost had a clean shot on goal at close range.

Faded in the second half Strode inside on the ball in the late stages and earned Sibley a yellow card when he was taken down.

Helped Reading to drive the ball out of their half a few times in the first half when they were struggling to pass out.

Worked hard off the ball as well in the first half, having to do more of the dogswork when Wing is his midfield partner. Frayed a bit when pulled out of the structure.

Caught behind the ball a few too many times especially in the second half, leading to him having to foul a few times. That eventually saw Rinomhota booked for a fifth time this season and he will miss the next league game.

Suffered a bad moment when he failed to make a challenge on O'Donkor for the first goal, letting the shot travel through his legs.

Did deliver a lot of good set pieces today, providing chances for Marriott, O'Connor and Rinomhota from corners alone.

In danger of becoming a luxury player though, given that his set-piece delivery is excellent, but his open-play workrate is flagging. Wing still has more vision and ability than 21 other players in every game he plays, but his mobility does seem to be limiting him. Made just four defensive contributions today.

Lost the ball cheaply after one of his corners was cleared out, conceding a counter-attack to Oxford with Reading's defenders behind the ball. In an unfortunate image, smashed a late chance to shoot from outside of the box well over the bar.

Found himself with very light marking in the opening 10 minutes, and was almost able to capitalise, slinging one low cross into the box that deserved a Reading boot.

Oxford tightened up after Lisbie helped created a second chance by earning a free-kick, limiting his space for the rest of the first period

Strode forward through the middle toward the end of the first period, beating a man and laying off the ball for a shot on Marriott's left foot.

Kept working hard after half-time, earning Reading a corner with a nice dribble down the right flank. Booked unnecessarily at the end of the game for a late challenge.

Couldn't find much time on the ball so had to influence the game off it. Raised the temperature by standing over a man he had fouled midway through the first half. Thoroughly rattled the Oxford captain Brannagan in the process.

Eventually booked at the end of the half for leaving one on Brannagan. Found space on the edge of the box for a shot, but hooked his left footed effort well over the bar.

Put in a more muted performance in the second half and was hooked in a full switch of the attack shortly before Oxford's goals.

Almost got a toe onto Lisbie's low cross in the opening minutes of the game, in what would have been a perfect return to the team.

Did really well at the start of the second half to anticipate a low cross in the box, clearing it out to Marriott.

Made another great interception at the other end of the pitch on the hour mark, jumping on a clearance from the goalie and almost springing Stokes loose in the box.

Picked up his first start since his recent injury and continued to do what he does: generate shots for Reading.

Tried his first shot of the day with an ambitious overhead kick. Stung the goalkeeper's palms with a strong effort on his left foot at the end of the first half.

Met a second-half corner at the near post but couldn't keep the headed effort down. Withdrawn on the 70-minute mark to avoid further injury concerns but is far superior to any other player Reading can call upon up top.

Hooked the ball off the bar shortly after coming on, unlucky not to be rewarded with his fifth goal of the season. Couldn't find the ball in the box after that though, failing to get another shot away.

Caught out leaving the back post exposed for the second Oxford goal. After getting wound up in an arm fight with his man to mark, Brown ended up not facing the right way when the ball arrived in the box.

Brought on to help Reading find a winner but immediately had his assignment changed to "find an equaliser".

Unable to really affect that change, touching the ball only five times in the match. Got closest to the goal sliding in to meet a cross late on, but couldn't find a way through the bundle of Oxford and Reading bodies.

Went out to the left to replace kyerey: the man who stole his job tonight. Didn't do much to suggest that was the wrong decision but had very limited time on the field to make an impact.

Replaced Rinomhota late on but was unable to get onto the ball much with Oxford looking to see the game out.

articles.title: Joe Scarborough goes after ESPN’s Pat McAfee: ‘It is a shame for the viewer’
articles.summary: He contends ESPN can run its company how it wants.
articles.body:
Pat McAfee is a problem for ESPN's "College GameDay," Joe Scarborough of "Morning Joe" hammered away at Tuesday during election day.

McAfee's recent headline-grabbing issues with the University of Utah was the tipping point.

"I've just had enough of this Pat McAfee ruining 'College GameDay,'" Scarborough said Tuesday. "I look forward to waking up on Saturday mornings and watching that. ... It's like he's melting down. ...

"It's really ESPN. I mean, they run their company the way they want to run their company, but man, it is a shame for the viewer."

McAfee revealed there have been death threats against him as a result of the controversy surrounding ESPN's "College GameDay" visit to Utah.

"I've stayed away from my mentions and DMs this month since these back to back days but ... I'm sure if I went in there now, I'd find some wishes for and threats of death for me," McAfee posted on X. "'Don't read them.' They're everywhere."

The post includes screenshots from direct messages threatening violence against him and tweets expressing a desire to see him dead.

The issue, according to Scarborough, is the show has gotten away from college football being played on Saturday and it's more about itself.

"I love watching Rece (Davis)," he said. "I love watching those guys and watching Nick (Saban) on there talking. ... Kirk Herbstreit's amazing. Desmond (Howard) — they're all great. And they're all being eclipsed by ESPN's just insatiable desire to give this guy more time."

"Maybe you aren't having to be yelling at people and being freaked out because two kids in Utah put up signs or say something that might offend you," Scarborough said.

Meanwhile, McAfee said he felt "uncomfortable" after the University of Utah posted a since-deleted video of students "dogging" him. He also said the video shared by the university account was inciteful against him.

McAfee cited the visit to the University of Utah reminded him of assassination of Charlie Kirk .

"I do get a bit (expletive) up when a couple days after The New York Times releases a 'WE ARE ALLOWED TO AND SHOULD HATE THIS GUY' piece, a university puts a video out from their own page, indicating, 'We think he's a corny creep here.' It's a weird time," McAfee posted. "The things that get said about what my daughter and son and wife deserve are all rather wild as well."

McAfee cited an experience ahead of "College GameDay" in Knoxville, Tennessee, in 2025 — the show's first episode after Kirk was killed.

He said security concerns arose about a potential "copycat" scenario, as "GameDay" was "the next huge gathering on a campus."
